items.title: ✨ feat(cove): CoVe 2.x hardening — confidence gate, date anchoring, enforceable least-privilege
items.body:
## Summary

Hardens the `cove` skill (Agentic CoVe 2.0) on both deliverables — the agent-native SKILL.md protocol and the Python reference pipeline — closing the gaps found in a full audit of the skill.

### SKILL.md + bundled agent

- **Enforceable least privilege**: ship `cove/agents/cove-verifier.md` (tool allowlist: `WebSearch, WebFetch` only). Claude Code's default `general-purpose` subagent has ALL tools, so the previous "grant only web search" instruction was aspirational; SKILL now says to dispatch the bundled restricted agent when installed and honestly labels the prompt-level fallback as instructive, not enforced. READMEs (zh/en) updated to match.
- **Confidence gate (Phase 3)**: corrections require High/Medium-confidence evidence; a Low-confidence contradiction yields a caveat + Uncertain, never a rewrite.
- **Date anchoring (Phase 1)**: freshness-sensitive claims (latest version / current status / prices) must embed today's date in the `verification_query`.
- **Docs-tool routing (Phase 2)**: version-sensitive library/API claims prefer a documentation retrieval tool (e.g. Context7) over generic web search.
- **Confidence calibration**: High requires ≥2 independent agreeing sources or 1 authoritative primary source; verifier `Sources` list only URLs that ground the answer.
- **No silent truncation**: claims dropped by the >10 cap must be listed under "Skipped" in the Verification Summary.
- **Language rules**: revised response stays in the draft's language; queries use the language most likely to yield authoritative sources.
- Frontmatter: `argument-hint` + `disable-model-invocation: true` (manual `/cove` only; both verified against current Claude Code docs).

### Reference pipeline (`cove/reference/`)

- **Per-claim error degradation**: one verifier failure (search outage, provider error) degrades that claim to a conservative "unable to verify" instead of aborting all of Phase 2.
- **Truncation guard**: `AnthropicLLM` `max_tokens` is configurable (default 4096, was hardcoded 2048); `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` raises instead of silently flowing a cut-off draft/revision downstream.
- **Citation precision**: verifier reports `Supported-by:` evidence numbers, so claim sources contain only the supporting URLs (explicit "none" → empty; missing line → conservative fallback to all).
- **Evidence-aware finalize**: Phase 3 receives short evidence quotes, not just verifier verdicts, and its prompt gates corrections on confidence.
- **Retry feedback**: Phase 1's single JSON retry feeds the validation error back to the model; `run()`/`phase1_plan()` gain `today=` for date anchoring.
- deep/shallow verification merged into one `asyncio.gather` (removes the sequential barrier).

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` in `cove/reference`: **42 passed** (was 30; +12 regression tests covering degradation, `Supported-by` parsing/fallback, truncation, retry feedback, date anchoring, and the new prompt-constraint locks)
- [x] SKILL.md frontmatter parses; Phase 3 output template code-block structure verified
- [ ] Post-merge: re-deploy to consumers (`npx skills add RayChang/agent-skills@cove` in fvg / alibi) — project-level copies do not update on repo merge

items.title: fix(sast): eliminate 2 residual precision-suite FPs at engine level (0.895 -> 1.00)
items.body:
## Summary

The honest SAST precision suite scored **precision 0.895 / recall 1.00 / F1 0.944** (17 TP, 2 FP, 0 FN). This PR eliminates both residual false positives **at the engine level** (no file exclusion, no corpus curation), taking the suite to **precision 1.00 / recall 1.00 / F1 1.00** (17 TP, 0 FP, 0 FN), noise ratio 0.00.

## FP #1 — `clean_svg_blob.ts`: SEC-161 entropy inside a decoded SVG

**Root cause:** The secrets decode-and-scan path (`DecodeAndScan`) base64-decodes embedded blobs and re-scans the decoded bytes, but those decoded findings are added directly via `fs.Add` and bypass the lexctx data-blob filter the main scan applies. A base64 `data:image/svg+xml` blob decodes to SVG markup whose long alphanumeric runs trip the entropy rules (SEC-161/162/163).

**Fix:** `DecodeAndScan` now drops entropy-only findings when the decoded content is itself a markup/image/data blob (SVG/XML/HTML markup or an image magic header). A real secret hidden in base64 decodes to a bare credential — not markup — so provider pattern rules still catch it. Tested both ways: SVG-in-base64 suppressed; `AKIA...`-in-base64 still found.

## FP #2 — `tp_ssti.py`: TAINT-003 double-reports the SSTI

**Root cause:** `render_template_string` is a legitimate SSTI sink (TAINT-003, `vuln_class: ssti`) and is *also* matched by the `VARIANT-005` CVE signature. Both fire on the same line — one real vulnerability reported twice; the annotation designates VARIANT-005 as canonical, so TAINT-003 scores as a FP.

**Fix:** New `FindingSet.SuppressDuplicateVulnClass` (wired into `refineFindings`) drops a taint finding when another analyzer already reports the same `vuln_class` at the same file+line, keeping the more specific CVE signature. Variants signatures now carry an optional `vuln_class` (`ssti` on VARIANT-005) so the dedup is class-based, not rule-ID-hardcoded. It is class-scoped: an XSS taint finding is only ever suppressed by another XSS finding at the same span — it never hides a distinct vulnerability and never weakens XSS detection.

## Baseline + docs

- Ratcheted `testdata/precision-suite/baseline.json` to the 1.00 floor; `TestPrecisionSuiteBaseline` passes.
- Updated `testdata/precision-suite/README.md` headline numbers (now 1.00/1.00/1.00, noise 0.00, density 1.06) and marked items 5–6 resolved.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./core/taint/... ./core/analyzers/...` — all green.
- golangci-lint clean on changed packages (only pre-existing `hugeParam` on untouched code, filtered by CI `only-new-issues`).
- Self-scan gate: PR introduces **zero** new findings (identical finding set to `main`).

**Before → after: precision 0.895 → 1.00, recall 1.00 → 1.00, F1 0.944 → 1.00 (TP 17, FP 2 → 0, FN 0).**

items.title: [TRON]: Simply implementation
items.body:
**New package `@guardian-sdk/tron`** (FullNode HTTP API only — no TronGrid; TronWeb builds txs, signs locally):
  - **Staking lifecycle** — freeze/vote/unfreeze/claim mapped onto the SDK contracts:
    | SDK tx | Tron contract |
    |---|---|
    | `Delegate` (+ `resource`) | `FreezeBalanceV2` |
    | `Undelegate` | `UnfreezeBalanceV2` |
    | `Vote` *(new)* | `VoteWitnessContract` |
    | `ClaimDelegate` | `WithdrawExpireUnfreeze` (principal) |
    | `ClaimRewards` | `WithdrawBalance` (rewards) |
  - **`getDelegations`** — resource-granular, exposing the full `Frozen → Active → Pending → Claimable` lifecycle (freezing alone earns nothing
  until you vote; placeholder validator for un-voted/unbonding positions).
  - **`getBalances`** — `Available` / `Staked` / `Pending` / `Claimable` / `Rewards`, no double-counting.
  - **`getValidators`** — Super Representatives with **computed APR** (Tron has no APY endpoint), 3-min cache.
  - **Resource-aware `estimateFee`** — returns **0 fee** when the account's bandwidth covers the tx, else a real shortfall burn. Also enforces
  balance-aware validation (over-vote past Tron Power, unfreeze > frozen, freeze > balance) client-side.
  - **Signing** — `sign` / `prehash` / `compile` (secp256k1 over `txID`; owner derived from the signing key).

  **Shared `@guardian-sdk/sdk` additions (additive, back-compat):**
  - `VoteTransaction` + `"Vote"` in `TransactionType`
  - `"Frozen"` `DelegationStatus` (Tron-only, like `"Claimable"` is BSC-only)
  - `ResourceFee` in the `Fee` union
  - `validator` made optional on `Delegate`/`Undelegate` + `assertValidator` guard (BSC/Cardano call sites guarded — runtime invariant
  preserved)

  **Docs & plumbing:** `.claude/rules/tron.md` mechanics explainer, `packages/tron/README.md`, runnable
  `examples/tron-native-staking-sample.ts`, root `CLAUDE.md`/build/test-script updates, and a changeset (`@guardian-sdk/sdk` minor +
  `@guardian-sdk/bsc` patch — `tron`/`cardano` excluded to respect the changeset ignore list).

  ## Units & mechanics
  All amounts in **SUN** (1 TRX = 10⁶, decimals 6). 14-day unbonding; rewards do **not** auto-compound (manual claim, 24h cooldown); partial
  unstaking supported (unlike Cardano).

  ## Testing
  - `pnpm run build`, `typecheck`, `test`, `lint`, `format:check`, and `npx tsc -p examples/tsconfig.json` — all green.
  - 50 Tron unit tests (fetch-mocked RPC, deterministic fixtures) covering account mapping, delegation lifecycle, balances, APR, validations,
  tx-builder, resource-aware fees, and sign/prehash/compile.
  - No change to BSC (62) / Cardano (167) test outcomes.

  ## Follow-ups (non-blocking, alpha)
  - APR `sr_block_rewards` term carries a `[VERIFY]` caveat — validate against real on-chain numbers.
  - RPC number→bigint funnels through JS `number` (precision ceiling ~9M TRX) — revisit if whale balances are expected.

  ## Release note
  `@guardian-sdk/tron` is `alpha` and in the changeset `ignore` list — it does **not** auto-release with `sdk`/`bsc`.

items.title: v0.7.0: controlled-mutation benchmark; retire owner-checked evidence narrative
items.body:
Replaces the prior private-review benchmark narrative with a numbers-only,
known-truth **controlled-mutation benchmark**, and lets the public repo's
numbers speak for themselves.

## Benchmark (`dorian bench mutation`, `docs/BENCHMARK_v0.6.0.md`)
41 (artifact, mutation) pairs over one invented, synthetic fixture, 9 claims;
every label is a mechanical consequence of the edit (frozen before measurement —
no human/model/panel judgment). dorian vs two file-change-watcher baselines:

| detector | precision | recall | FP |
|---|---|---|---|
| naive file-watcher | 0.49 | 1.00 | 20 |
| line-aware watcher | 0.56 | 1.00 | 15 |
| dorian | 0.76 | 0.84 | 5 |

False-positive reduction 4.0x (naive) / 3.0x (line-aware). dorian trades recall
(3 substring-checker misses) for precision; the gap holds against the line-aware
baseline. Numbers are specific to this fixture — a mechanism demonstration, not a
universal claim. Deterministic output; in-fixture bootstrap CIs.

## Cleanup
- Remove the owner-review / public-summary pipeline and its tests.
- Archive the superseded v0.0 records under `archive/`; delete the dead how-to.
- Scrub reviewer/agent/owner evidence wording from README, docs, and tests
  (both grep gates clean on the tracked surface; `bench/real/` stays gitignored).
- README benchmark section is now numbers-only.

## Validation
- `ruff` clean; **439 tests pass**; `make bench` (selftest replay) intact.
- New tests: determinism, output schema, pre-registered confusion matrix,
  public-wording gate, no private/host leakage, README has no owner-checked claim.

  Enabling `float_roundtrip` will use sufficient precision when parsing fixed precision floats from JSON to ensure that they maintain accuracy when round-tripped through JSON. This comes at an approximately 2x performance cost for parsing floats compared to the default best-effort precision.

  Unlike `arbitrary_precision`, the new `float_roundtrip` feature makes f64 -> JSON -> f64 produce output identical to the input. `arbitrary_precision` is for making JSON -> serde\_json::Number -> JSON produce output identical to the input.

<br>

##### Compatibility notes

Part of the improvement to compile time comes from having generic methods in serde\_json instantiate many fewer Visitor trait methods than they used to. For example if a Deserialize impl is being deserialized from JSON and the impl indicates to Serde that the type u64 is expected, serde\_json can avoid instantiating all of the Visitor methods that deal with string, borrowed string, unit, sequence, map, boolean, char, bytes, borrowed bytes, option, newtype, and enum. Previously *all* of these methods were instantiated and compile times were predictably poor in consequence. As of this release, serde\_json instantiates only the expected Visitor methods and instead renders invalid\_type error messages in a central place in the Deserializer that can be instantiated just once. This does not apply to deserialize\_any for which it continues to be necessary to instantiate every Visitor method.

This does mean that code relying on the deserialize hint to be *wrong* may no longer deserialize successfully.

```rust
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for MyType {
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
        where D: Deserializer<'de>
    {
        struct MyVisitor;

        impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for MyVisitor {
            type Value = MyType;

            fn expecting(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
                f.write_str("a string, although we ask the deserializer for u64")
            }

            fn visit_str<E>(self, v: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, E>
                where E: de::Error
            {
                Ok(/* ... */)
            }
        }

        // It used to be that serde_json would ignore this hint and call visit_str
        // for string input, but in the general case that destroys compile times
        // by instantiating far more Visitor methods than are ever used.
        deserializer.deserialize_u64(MyVisitor)
    }
}
```

items.title: Prose to checks: pair the two tiers' geohash known-vector suites
items.body:
One conversion from the `prose-to-checks-sweep` run of 2026-07-28 over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the binding scope). Logged on the tracker, #22.

## The prose

`RULES.md` §"Two encoders, one contract" carried an always-testable half as prose:

> the known-vector suites on both sides ... carry the *same* vectors deliberately; touching either encoder means re-running both, **and extending one vector list means extending the other**.

Nothing enforced that last clause. Add a vector to `app/test/geohash_test.dart` and not to `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts` (or the reverse) and **both suites stay green** — different languages, different runners, different CI jobs — while the compatibility claim silently stops covering that coordinate. The two encoders only meet in those two files, and the two files never meet at all.

## Why this one is a check and not a test in disguise

It asserts nothing about what either encoder *does*. It compares two committed tables of literals that must agree — the same static-signature shape as this pack's existing `cross-tier-constants` guard, which pairs declarations across two files that cannot share an import. The encoders' *behavioural* agreement stays prose, because no post-hoc scan can run one encoder against the other; that is precisely what the suites themselves are for.

## The check

`shouts-and-whispers/geohash-vector-parity` (blocking). It **parses rather than greps**: only assertions written at the shared production precision 9 are read — the client's default-precision `encode(lat, lng)` calls and the server's explicit `geohashForLocation([lat, lng], 9)` calls — so the deliberately unpaired cases (the client's precision 1/5/11/12 vectors, the server's 10-char default-precision ones) are never mistaken for drift. Coordinates compare as numbers, not spelling.

It fires when:
- either suite carries a precision-9 coordinate the other lacks (both directions),
- the two suites expect **different** hashes for the same coordinate,
- a suite is unreadable or stops carrying precision-9 vectors at all (the staleness guard this pack's other checks also carry — a guard that quietly stops guarding is worse than none).

## See-it-fail

Mandatory and done twice over. Seven fixtures in `pack.test.mjs` (fixtures 9 → 16, all passing), **and** additionally verified red against mutations of the *real* suites — a client-only vector, a server-only vector, and a one-character hash drift each produce exactly one finding; the unmutated tree is quiet.

## Prose trimmed

The §"Two encoders, one contract" enforcement clause is now rationale only: why a one-sided vector is invisible, and why the encoding agreement itself cannot be scanned. The pack `README.md` tables and fixture count are updated to match.

## Scope

Confined to `.claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers` — one new module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixtures, and the trimmed prose. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` (the read-only mounted canon) is touched, and no rule an existing check already covers was re-converted.

Offline suite green: `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/pack.test.mjs` 16/16, `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both clean.

items.body:
Bumps [meshoptimizer](https://github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer) from 1.1.1 to 1.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from meshoptimizer's releases.

v1.2

This release introduces a major new feature, tangent frame generation, significantly improves vertex decoding performance on Intel/AMD CPUs and also adds several smaller features and improvements. Highlights:

A new tangent frame generator can generate tangents from either indexed or unindexed triangle mesh with positions/normals/texture coordinates. The generator implements MikkTSpace algorithm, but is significantly faster to run (~6-10x faster than mikktspace.c depending on the input structure). Note that the generation result is a per-corner tangent and applying the tangents to the indexed mesh may require splitting source vertices; consult documentation for details. By default, the algorithm uses a modified weighting scheme that significantly improves tangent quality around beveled regions in the mesh, with meshopt_TangentCompatible option provided for cases where exact compatibility with mikktspace.c is important (e.g. normal map baking workflows).

Vertex decoding (meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer) implementation for Intel/AMD CPUs has been significantly revised. The new mostly branchless SSSE3 implementation is usually ~20-45% faster than it was in previous releases, with the gains depending on CPU and the data composition; it's typical to see gains in the upper half of this range for engine-packed data. This implementation is automatically selected on compatible CPUs (SSSE3+POPCNT), with no change in data encoding, so to get this performance boost a library update is sufficient. If the code is compiled with AVX-512/AVX10 support (which is currently only selected at compile time when opted into), the decoding is an additional ~10% faster.

Additionally, new index filtering functions are provided to remove degenerate/duplicate triangles based on positional identity, which can be especially helpful for raytracing performance, a function for computing optimal shared exponent for cluster positions can be used to prepare geometry for upcoming DXR2 Compressed1 format, and clusterlod.h now implements DAG BVH construction via clodBuildHierarchy.

The majority of the work on the core library in this release has been sponsored by Valve; thank you!

Library improvements

  • New experimental function for generating tangents based on MikkTSpace algorithm, meshopt_generateTangents
  • New experimental functions for filtering out degenerate and duplicate triangles based on positional identity, meshopt_filterIndexBuffer/meshopt_filterIndexBufferMulti
  • New experimental function for computing optimal shared exponent for cluster positions which can be used with upcoming DXR2 Compressed1 format
  • meshopt_encode/decodeMeshlet* functions, meshopt_extractMeshletIndices and meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel functions, as well as meshopt_SimplifyVertex_Priority and meshopt_SimplifyRegularizeLight flags, are now stable.
  • Significantly improve meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer performance on existing data for Intel/AMD CPUs (20-45% faster depending on CPU and data characteristics)
  • Significantly improve performance of meshopt_partitionClusters on larger partition sizes (~2x for target_size 64, ~200x for 1024)
  • Improve post-compression ratio for meshlets encoded using meshlet codec after meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel with level 1+ (~0.5% gains)
  • Fix reduced encoding precision of small numbers when using meshopt_encodeFilterExp with a shared exponent mode if the input contains exact zeroes
  • Support special meshlet hardware configurations that require a limited triangle index span via MESHOPTIMIZER_CLUSTERIZER_INDEXLIMIT define
  • Support direct decoding of vertex data into destination buffer via MESHOPTIMIZER_VERTEXCODEC_ZEROCOPY define for slightly faster decoding (disabled by default as it does not work well with write-combined memory)

Additional improvements

  • clusterlod.h now implements DAG BVH construction via clodBuildHierarchy for efficient hierarchical cut selection
  • Add tangent generation to gltfpack when requested via -gt argument
  • Add experimental MeshoptTangents JavaScript module with the new tangent space generator
  • Fix meshopt_decoder.js Wasm SIMD implementation corner case when using v1 format and highest compression (part of 1.1.1 patch release)
  • Fix a rare race condition in meshopt_decoder.js when using WebWorkers via useWorkers (part of 1.1.1 patch release)
  • Improve vertex decoding performance in meshopt_decoder.js by 5-10%
  • Fix several bugs in gltfpack (mesh merging with negative scales no longer flips tangent frames, more careful handling of animation tracks with zero scale)

items.title: fix(kneeboard): bullseye cue + populated STPT on SEAD/DEAD target page
items.body:
## What

Fixes the SEAD/DEAD kneeboard target page (`SeadTaskPage`):

- **STPT was always blank.** Targets were paired to their per-target
  `TARGET_POINT` waypoint by exact x/y position, which never matches under
  Approximate target intel (the player waypoint is deliberately offset from the
  unit). Now paired **by order** — both the listed targets and the waypoints
  derive from the same `strike_targets` sequence — so STPT stays populated in
  both Exact and Approximate modes.
- **Cue is now a rough bullseye.** Replaced the static
  `"Search around target area waypoint"` text with `Bullseye <brg> for <nm>`:
  true bearing rounded to the nearest degree, range to the nearest nautical
  mile (~1 NM accuracy). DEAD always uses the cue; SEAD keeps exact DMS coords
  unless Approximate intel is on.

## Why

On the DEAD target page the STPT column came up empty for every row and the Cue
was a non-actionable "search the area" string, so players had no waypoint
reference and no quick geographic anchor. The bullseye cue keeps the
"acquire-it-yourself" intent of Approximate intel while giving a usable
search start point, and the order-based pairing makes the steerpoint numbers
reliable regardless of intel precision.

## Reviewer notes

- **Bearing is _true_, not magnetic** (matches the existing flight-plan page
  convention). If the squadron expects magnetic bullseye calls, this needs
  theater magnetic variation applied — flag it and I'll change it.
- **Not CI-runnable in-game.** The Lua/mission side can't be exercised here.
  Needs an in-game pass to confirm STPT numbers match the jet's steerpoints and
  the bullseye points within ~1 NM of each target.
- Tests updated for the new `SeadTaskPage(flight, bullseye, dark)` signature and
  row shape; README.md + docs/dev/414th-features.md §5 synced.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/missiongenerator/test_kneeboard_task_pages.py` — pass
- `black --check .` — clean
- `mypy game tests` — no issues (509 files)

items.title: feat(decode): pure-Python RAIF decoder with differential parity
items.body:
## Summary
- Adds `src/raif_decode.py` — a dependency-free (stdlib-only) Python port of the canonical TypeScript `decode` / `decodeLenient` from `raif-standard`. The model emits RAIF, not JSON, so every Python consumer needs a decode step at the output boundary; this removes the need for a `bun` subprocess in the hot path.
- Ports the **full decode path**: the repair pipeline (markdown fences, mode markers, CRLF, multi-line brace flattening, nonce-block recovery, relaxed openers, array literals, tables, inline objects, repeated-key indexing, sparse-array rejection), optional schema-typed decode, and the encode round-trip throw-gate that TS `decode` applies. The encoder itself is not ported (decode never needs it); `fix`/`validate` are out of scope.
- Documents the decode boundary and parity guarantees in the README.

## Why
RAIF is a deterministic codec, but the only canonical decoder lived in TypeScript — every Python consumer had to shell out to `bun`. This gives Python harnesses a native, drop-in `decode()` returning `{"ok", "value"/"error", "repairs"}`, plus `decode_lenient()` for per-leaf recovery.

## How equivalence is enforced
Two independent harnesses pin the port to the TS engine as ground truth:
- `src/test_raif_decode.py` — parity over the full corpus (**21,240** real RAIF strings).
- `src/test_raif_differential.py` — differential fuzzing via the `_raif_oracle.py` bun bridge: random objects round-tripped through the real TS encoder (both emission profiles), then degraded by mutations targeting every repair branch (truncation, fences/markers, CRLF, nonce/delimiter, brace-flatten, schema-typed, pure garbage), asserting `decode_py(x) == decode_ts(x)` for every `x`.

Fuzzing + a Codex audit surfaced and pinned several JS/Python semantic divergences, now matched to the TS engine:
- encode round-trip gate — keys containing `<<<`/`>>>` must reject;
- regex `.` line-terminator set (`\r`/LS/PS) differs JS vs Python;
- whitespace set for trims/blank-checks (NEL, C0 separators, BOM);
- `\d` Unicode digits vs ASCII (ASCII-gated all numeric/index regexes);
- IEEE-754 double precision + overflow rejection for numbers;
- UTF-16 code-unit sort order for the repeated-keys repair detail.

Only intentional, documented difference: large integral numbers print as Python ints vs JS exponential — numerically equal as doubles.

## Test plan
- [x] `python src/test_raif_decode.py` — 21,240/21,240 corpus inputs match the TS decoder
- [x] `python src/test_raif_differential.py` — 13/13 differential properties hold
- [x] Direct `bun` verification of every audit finding — 0 divergences
- [ ] CI / reviewer: requires a sibling `raif-standard` checkout with `bun install` in `prototype/` for the parity tests (they skip cleanly when absent); the decoder module itself is stdlib-only

## Notes
- The decoder module has zero runtime dependencies and is independent of the training stack.
- The parity/differential tests need the sibling `raif-standard` repo + `bun` only to run; the shipped `raif_decode.py` does not.

items.title: feat(eval): falsify the thesis. semantic-dedup harness, curated dataset, honest results
items.body:
## goal

prove or disprove the product thesis with measurement, not anecdote.

the claim 'semantic intent dedup catches real llm retries reliably and safely' was demonstrated on hand-crafted near-duplicates but never measured against precision and recall. operators had no way to tune semantic_threshold except by guessing. this pr ships the harness, the dataset, the numbers, and the policy defaults that the numbers point at.

## what is in the pr

- new internal/eval package mirrors the proxy's normalize+fingerprint+intent-string code so the eval cannot drift from production behavior. Runner scores every pair, BuildPairs walks every same-tool combination, Evaluate sweeps thresholds across [0.50, 0.99] in 0.01 steps, BestThreshold picks highest f1 per tool with a tie-break toward conservative thresholds.
- new cmd/potent-eval cli. accepts a jsonl dataset and a policy yaml, emits a human table or json document.
- new docs/eval/dataset.jsonl. 51 records, 5 tools (send_email, charge_card, create_task, delete_user, search_web), 4-8 intents per tool, each with whitespace, reorder, synonym, and paraphrase variants, plus adversarial negatives that share template words with positives but differ on a load-bearing field (different recipient, different amount, opposite verb, different priority, different topic).
- new docs/eval/methodology.md describes how the dataset was built and what it does not test.
- new docs/eval/results.md ships the honest numbers and a per-tool recommendation.
- ci workflow gains a semantic-eval job that runs the harness on every push and uploads the json artifact for regression tracking.
- configs/policy.yaml semantic_threshold values updated from guessed defaults to calibrated values, with comments pointing at the methodology.
- readme replaces 'semantic catches llm retries' with a section that links to the results and notes the precision/recall tradeoff.

## the headline numbers

| tool | best threshold | precision | recall | fpr | f1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| send_email | 0.73 | 0.559 | 1.000 | 0.128 | 0.717 |
| charge_card | 0.91 | 0.375 | 0.750 | 0.156 | 0.500 |
| create_task | 0.85 | 0.462 | 0.857 | 0.241 | 0.600 |
| delete_user | 0.99 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.000 | 1.000 |
| search_web | 0.81 | 0.625 | 0.455 | 0.055 | 0.526 |

at threshold 0.9 (the readme's prior default) send_email recall drops to 0.263. the embedder misses 74% of paraphrases an llm would realistically produce. for charge_card the semantic tier produces 5 false positives at any reasonable threshold. for short queries (search_web) recall caps at 0.455 below a 10% fpr.

## honest verdict

the mechanism works as designed. whitespace/casing/reorder retries are caught reliably. paraphrases are caught partially. for structured/numeric tools the semantic tier is at best neutral and at worst harmful. the readme's pre-1.0 admission about the hashing-tfidf limits is validated by the data. onnx swap is the next step and this eval will be rerun when it ships.

## test plan

- [x] go test -race -cover ./...  all packages >= 80%; eval at 87.9%
- [x] go vet / staticcheck / gosec clean
- [x] make eval reproduces the numbers in docs/eval/results.md
- [x] make eval-json emits valid json
- [x] curated dataset parses without errors
- [x] new TestLoadDataset_DatasetFile_IsValid asserts the dataset has at least 30 records and every record has tool+intent_id+args
- [x] ci semantic-eval job runs the harness on push
- [ ] after merge: cut v0.1.9 to publish the eval and the new policy defaults

items.title: Curate FDC's own category into GPC, and grade every match by confidence
items.body:
Deep-dives further into the "how much does GPC match OFF and FDC" analysis from the previous conversation, and builds the fix — starting with FDC, as requested.

## The diagnosis (documented in full in ARCH.md, "GPC Category Matching")

The only GPC matcher used OFF's free-text tags, fuzzy-matched with `LIKE '%label%'`. On the real local corpus it hit **44.9%** of OFF products with a category — and a manual audit found **69% of those hits were noise**: `en:beverages` substring-matched the brick *"Alcoholic Beverages Variety Packs"*, misclassifying 110,000+ products including plain pasta. Three causes, each independently confirmed:

1. **Wrong tag order** — OFF orders tags broad→narrow; the code tried the broadest (least specific) three first.
2. **Substring matching, no word boundaries.**
3. **Even fixed, a real precision ceiling remains** — polysemous words (`beans`: coffee vs. legume) and OFF vocabulary GPC's ~730-word brick descriptions don't contain at all (`flageolet`).

**FDC's own category was a separate, bigger gap: never even consulted.** `usda_data["category"]` (100% populated) was ignored entirely — every FDC-only product got an empty `category_hierarchy` no matter how good a match its own category would have made.

## The fix: FDC and OFF get different treatment, because they have different shapes

FDC's `branded_food_category` is a **closed, controlled vocabulary** — 350 values, Pareto-distributed (top 20 = 48.7% of all branded foods, top 90 = 90.7%). Small and stable enough to **hand-verify**. `app/core/gpc_match.py` adds a 49-entry curated table — every brick code looked up and read against the real GPC taxonomy, not guessed — covering **67.4% of all FDC foods**.

Categories with no clean GPC equivalent are **deliberately excluded**, not forced onto an approximate brick (`Soda` — GPC has no carbonated-drink brick at all; `Nut & Seed Butters`; several "Other X" catch-alls), and documented as exclusions so nobody re-adds a guess later.

One bonus finding: FDC's own data has **two inconsistent spellings** of its baby-food category (a double space vs. a hyphenated variant) — both mapped.

OFF's tags have no closed vocabulary to curate — improving that matcher is future work, out of scope here.

## Confidence, exposed to the caller

```json
"category_hierarchy_source": "fdc_curated" | "off_fuzzy" | "none"
```

- `fdc_curated` — hand-verified, high confidence
- `off_fuzzy` — real matches, not individually verified — a hint, not ground truth
- `none` — nothing classified it; `category_hierarchy` may still show OFF's *raw* tags as a last resort, but that's an upstream label, not a GPC match, which is why the source stays `none`

The curated path is tried first; on a hit, the fuzzy path is **skipped outright**, not run and discarded. A future `reviewed` tier (human-checked `off_fuzzy` matches) is documented, not implemented.

## Verified live

```
Doritos (FDC category "Snacks")     -> Snacks Other                          source: fdc_curated
Hershey's (FDC category "Chocolate") -> Chocolate and Chocolate/Sugar Candy…  source: fdc_curated
```

Checked against the *actual* stored FDC category strings, not assumed.

## Tests

17 new: table integrity + lookup + hierarchy resolution (`test_gpc_match.py`), and orchestrator priority (`test_orchestrator_merge.py`) — curated wins and skips fuzzy, falls back when uncurated, falls back with no FDC data, raw-tag fallback stays `none`, no-categories stays `none`. Plus fixture fixes for the new `food_category` field FDC records now carry. **Full suite: 732 passing**, flake8 clean.

## Docs

New ARCH.md section ("GPC Category Matching") with the full investigation — the false-positive audit, the three root causes, the strategy-comparison numbers, and why the precision ceiling can't be tuned away. SPECS.md and README updated to match.

items.title: bench(v1.6.0): scaffold honest-benchmark harness with spike gate
items.body:
Stage A of the v1.6.0 release plan — the harness that produces the public F1 / precision / recall numbers we'll stake credibility on. Stops short of actually running the spike (separate session — needs license key, locally-built ctxloom, and ~30 min runtime).

## What this enables

Once the spike runs and passes, ctxloom can publish a benchmark table like:

> On 6 reference OSS repos × 3 PRs each (18 PRs total), ctxloom's blast-radius achieves F1 X.XX, precision X.XX, recall X.XX, with X.X× token reduction over the naive read-everything baseline.
> 
> Full methodology in [evaluate/methodology.md]. Per-PR data + weaknesses in [evaluate/limitations.md].

That table is the credibility moat the [post-merge review](https://github.com/kodiii/ctxloom/pull/161) identified as critical before any HN / Reddit push.

## Pre-publication gate (locked)

This is the critical-path constraint. Before publishing **anything**:

1. `npm run bench:spike` runs against 2 repos (express + fastapi) × 2 PRs each
2. Gate verdict:
   - **F1 ≥ 0.50 AND recall ≥ 0.90** → proceed to full corpus
   - **0.40 ≤ F1 < 0.50** → investigate per-PR; fix or accept with explicit limitations
   - **F1 < 0.40 OR recall < 0.80** → STOP. Fix graph quality before bench. No publication.
3. Thresholds are written in code (\`scripts/bench/corpus.ts\` GATE const), not env vars — can't be moved at runtime.

Honest principles are documented in \`scripts/bench/README.md\` so the constraint outlives me:
- Don't cherry-pick PRs
- Don't tune thresholds to results
- Don't re-run for better numbers
- Publish the full per-PR table, not just aggregates

## What's in this PR

\`\`\`
scripts/bench/        — full harness (9 modules)
  types.ts            shared types (CorpusEntry, GroundTruth, BenchReport)
  corpus.ts           SPIKE_CORPUS, FULL_CORPUS, GATE thresholds
  groundTruth.ts      gh pr view → ground truth + entry point
  repoCheckout.ts     cached clones + worktrees ($BENCH_CACHE)
  predict.ts          shells to ctxloom CLI (index + blast-radius)
  metrics.ts          pure P/R/F1 functions (fully unit-tested)
  report.ts           Markdown emitter
  eval.ts             orchestrator with spike|full stage dispatch
  README.md           local docs + honest principles

evaluate/
  methodology.md      public methodology — locks corpus rules,
                      pipeline, tokenizer, ground-truth source,
                      gate logic. Will be linked from Show HN post.
  limitations.md      stub — gets concrete per-PR case studies
                      after the spike runs.

tests/BenchMetrics.test.ts — 14 tests covering perfect / none / over /
under prediction cases plus dedup and empty edges. All passing.

package.json — adds bench:spike, bench:full scripts.
\`\`\`

## What's deferred

- **Running the spike** — needs license key + local ctxloom + 30 min sustained runtime. Separate session, will report numbers + gate verdict.
- **Token-reduction measurement** — \`scripts/bench/tokens.ts\` is a TODO. The existing \`benchmarks/benchmark-public-repos.ts\` already measures aggregate token reduction; this harness focuses on F1/P/R first because those are the credibility gate. Tokens fold in after the spike passes.
- **CI workflow** (\`.github/workflows/bench.yml\`) — depends on \`CTXLOOM_LICENSE_KEY\` GitHub Actions secret being configured. Added once the spike confirms publishable numbers.
- **MCP JSON-RPC fallback in predict.ts** — if the \`ctxloom blast-radius\` CLI surface doesn't exist, predict.ts needs a child-process MCP harness. Marked TODO_CLI_SURFACE; built in the spike session if needed.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run lint\` — clean against project tsconfig
- [x] \`npx vitest run tests/BenchMetrics.test.ts\` — 14/14 passing
- [ ] After this lands: run \`npm run bench:spike\` end-to-end in a follow-up session, report gate verdict
- [ ] If gate passes: run \`npm run bench:full\`, publish \`evaluate/reports/summary.md\`, update README

## Related

- Strategic review that motivated this PR ordering: discussed in conversation
- Phase 0 host registry verification: #161
- Eventual v1.7.0 host adapters: blocked by v1.6.0 bench landing

items.title: Add web Database (sql.js + IndexedDB) to :web (M1 — resolves ADR 0001)
items.body:
Continues the PWA port with the item the roadmap flagged as **Next**: the deferred web `Database` seam — the last core **M1** platform service.

## What & why

Resolves [`docs/pwa-port/adr/0001-web-database.md`](../blob/claude/pwa-port-continue-inn766/docs/pwa-port/adr/0001-web-database.md) by implementing its **Option 3**: a synchronous SQLite via [sql.js](https://sql.js.org) (SQLite compiled to WebAssembly) run **in memory on the main thread**, with the database image persisted to **IndexedDB** (debounced) after each mutation and reloaded on startup.

Because sql.js is synchronous once loaded, the shared, *synchronous* `Database` interface is satisfied **unchanged** — which is the whole point of the port. The durable-at-scale path (data layer in a Web Worker over an OPFS sync-access VFS — ADR **Option 1**) stays the documented follow-up and slots in behind the same interface.

## Changes

- **`data/WebDatabase.kt`** — sql.js + IndexedDB interop boundary (all JS stays behind this file, like `WebMap`) plus the full `Database` impl: query/insert/update/delete/transaction, conflict algorithms, blob support. Values cross the boundary as JSON; blobs as base64.
- **`data/Database.kt`** — verbatim mirror of the shared `Database`/`CursorPosition`/`ConflictAlgorithm` interface (same rationale as `map/LatLon.kt`); deleted once `:web` compiles `:app`'s `commonMain` and `WebDatabase` binds to the real one.
- **`Main.kt` / `WebDatabaseHolder.kt`** — async DB bootstrap; binds it into Koin once ready (mirroring `AndroidModule`'s `single { AndroidDatabase(...) }`). Degrades gracefully to "no persistence" if sql.js can't load — same contract as the map.
- **`App.kt`** — demo exercises a representative slice of the real schema (NoteTable + spatial index, the blob-bearing WayGeometryTable), a typed-row round-trip, a **blob** round-trip, and a reload-surviving DB-backed launch counter.
- **`index.html`** loads sql.js from a CDN (like maplibre); **`sw.js`** cache bumped to `v3`.
- **`build.gradle.kts`** adds `kotlinx-serialization-json` (runtime JSON only, no compiler plugin — used as the marshalling format across the interop boundary).
- **Docs** — ADR 0001 → **Accepted**; ROADMAP + `web/README.md` updated.

## Notes / trade-offs

- **In-memory ceiling (documented):** the whole DB lives in memory and is flushed as one image — right for the preview and moderate data, **not** the full downloaded OSM dataset. That's what Option 1 (Worker + OPFS) is for.
- **Large integers:** sql.js returns integers as JS numbers, so values beyond 2^53 lose precision. Current OSM ids are within range; revisit with Option 1 / a BigInt-capable build before relying on larger ids.
- sql.js loads from a CDN and is not part of the offline shell yet; an offline launch comes up **without** persistence rather than crashing.

## Testing

I couldn't build locally (the dev environment's egress policy blocks the Gradle distribution and Google's Maven for Compose `androidx.*`). This PR relies on the `web-build.yml` CI job to compile and bundle the wasmJs target — runtime behavior is exercised by the demo screen as with M1/M2.

items.title: docs: refresh docs/ against the 2026-07-22..24 capability sweep

labels.name: auto-triaged
labels.description: Opened by an automated issue-sweep executor

items.body:
Documentation pass over `docs/` to match ~100 commits of capability change (2026-07-22 → 2026-07-24). Operator authorized editing `docs/**` explicitly ("review all our changes over the last few days and ensure docs and the website are updated to match"), which is the named-file permission `docs/*.md` requires. `briefs/`, `site/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/`, `package.json` and `report-template/findings.*.json` were not touched.

**Method:** every claim changed here was verified against the code or re-measured. Nothing was rewritten to match a summary. Where a doc was vague and I could not verify what is true, I left it and listed it below rather than inventing a confident sentence.

## 1. Stale paths — 26 files (#994)

#994 moved six functional docs out of `docs/`. Every citation is corrected: `docs/{scan-extras,fp-rules,quality-extras}.txt` → `briefs/`, `docs/audit-modules.md` → `briefs/audit-modules.md`, `docs/runbooks/anti-patterns.md` → `briefs/anti-patterns.md`, `docs/design/vuln-seam-app-answer-key.md` → `targets/vuln-seam-app/ANSWER-KEY.md`. Bare filename references in the operational docs were given their `briefs/` prefix so a reader can find them. `docs/runbooks/README.md` was still listing `anti-patterns.md` as one of its four runbooks; it now says where it went and why.

## 2. False capability claims corrected

Each was checked against the code before editing:

- **`design/m6-simplification-eval.md` §3 and `design/spec-72-crossmodule-corpus.md` §M6(c)** both stated there is no `Finding[]`-emitting scanner for M6. FALSE — `src/detectors/handrolled.ts` emits them with `precisionTier`, and `pnpm detector-census` measures **33** M6 detectors. The steelman survives and is now what the docs actually say: M6's *verdict* has no detector, and M6 has no `*.entries.ts` in the calibration corpus, so nothing about it is scored by `buildCoverageMatrix`. spec-72's revision note also still described the indicator layer as five shapes and claimed retry/backoff and pagination "did not graduate" — both graduated in #814 (confirmed in `briefs/quality-extras.txt`).
- **`design/deterministic-triage-ceiling-977.md`** recorded (a2) validator guards as needing `semgrep --pro` or a richer engine. #989 re-tested that premise and shipped the win in **semgrep OSS** (`pattern-sanitizers` + `by-side-effect: true`), recording a DON'T-BUY verdict. This is one of the four blockers the new verify-before-fix doctrine cites, so the correction names it as ASSUMED-written-as-MEASURED and points at the evaluation doc.
- **`design/benchproctor-evaluation.md`** cause #1 rested on "Harvey's SARIF carries a CWE tag on only ~12 distinct rules." #975 enriched all 92. Marked historical; the doc's own re-score addendum already carried the corrected conclusion, so only the mechanism needed flagging.
- **`design/carbon-scale-measurement.md`** carried three product findings that are no longer true: the cry-wolf **F (0/100)** is **A (97/100)** after #934 + #996 (27 findings before and after — nothing dropped); M10's "154 tables, Medium ceiling" is **214 tables, High ceiling** after #936's camelCase tokenization exposed 60 silently-NONE PII tables; and "M9 is not applicable" is false since #916–#918 (241 counted). All three kept as the historical reading with a dated update block, because the doc is a measurement record.
- **`design/vampi-m2-portability-measurement.md`** (4 gaps) and **`design/crapi-m2-portability-measurement.md`** (6 gaps) recorded harness gaps that #965 and #995/#966/#967 have closed — verified in `object-ids.ts`, `object-leak.ts`, `openapi-routes.ts`, `external-target.ts`, `discovery.ts` and `pentest.ts --mode=external`. Marked as records-of-measurement with a status block. **Honest caveat kept:** #965 was proven live against VAmPI, *not* re-run against crAPI's 8-container stack, so crAPI's specific shapes (`{order,payment}` envelope, `carId`) are covered by design and offline control, not by a live crAPI measurement. That is stated in the doc rather than smoothed over.
- **`docs/runbooks/m2-pentest-ops.md`** told operators Realtime has no channel-authorization probe and data residue is not probed. Both false since #951/#1003 and #907/#954/#956. Rewritten with the opt-in flag, the own-changes control, and the two live caveats (Broadcast/Presence unprobed #1029; first scoped table only — verified as `cfg.tables[0]` in `src/cli/pentest.ts` — #1030).
- **`docs/runbooks/full-engagement-run.md`** listed five "current" harness gaps (#523, #159, #161, #508, #514). All five are CLOSED per the tracker, and I verified #523's `--allow-target-install` exists in `run-audit.ts` rather than trusting the state alone. Also added a section for `pentest.ts --mode=external`, which had no runbook entry at all despite being the productized external-target path — including the scope rows an operator must read before writing a sentence about such a run.
- **`docs/m9-app-router.md`** and **`docs/free-tier-scope.md`** presented M9 as Next-only. Corrected to the framework-agnostic boundary model, with Astro/SvelteKit/Nuxt named as the still-not-assessed set. free-tier-scope also gained the SARIF/CycloneDX export flags (#867/#887), which it did not mention.
- **`docs/test-targets.md`** repeated carbon's F and 154-table figures, and gave inbox-zero's M9 baseline as 52 — it is **40** after #964's precision fix.

## 3. Numbers re-measured, not carried forward

Per doctrine I ran the gates rather than restating stored figures:

| Doc | Number | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `design/source-detector-recall.md`, `design/benchproctor-evaluation.md` | M1 mixed corpus (was `~198/201`) | `pnpm exec tsx src/cli/validate-calibration.ts` | **218/221** positives, **208/208** negatives, GATE PASS |
| `design/source-detector-recall.md` | source-recall + M9 tier | `pnpm exec tsx src/cli/validate-source-recall.ts` | 38/39 and 3/3 — both already correct, confirmed not changed |
| `design/spec-72-crossmodule-corpus.md`, `design/m6-simplification-eval.md` | M6 detector count | `pnpm detector-census` | **33** M6, 360 total |

Both places quoting the M1 figure now carry the date and an instruction to re-run rather than quote.

## 4. Provenance convention

Limitations I was already touching were tagged MEASURED (with command + date) or marked as historical readings, and given a falsifying command where one was obvious (`pnpm corpus-drift --target carbon`, `pentest.ts --mode=external`, `pnpm detector-census`). Not retrofitted across all 71 docs.

## CLAUDE.md sentences this work falsifies

I cannot edit CLAUDE.md. Two sentences need operator attention:

1. **"Sensitive paths" section, first bullet:** `- ` + "`docs/*.txt` and `docs/*.md` — the venture's briefs, positioning, and GTM strategy. Human-owned IP." — `docs/*.txt` no longer matches anything; #994 moved all three `.txt` briefs to `briefs/`. Recommended replacement: "`docs/*.md` and `docs/**/*.md` — the venture's positioning and GTM strategy. Human-owned IP. (`briefs/` is functional tool input, not prose — operator ruling 2026-07-24.)"

2. **The "Measure, don't recall" bullet's parenthetical:** "the last recorded measurement was 215/218 static positives, negatives 205/205 (measured 2026-07-24 after the #983–#991 detection batch…)". Re-measured today with the same command: **218/221 positives, 208/208 negatives** (the a2 validator-guard rules from #989 added +3/+3). The bullet's own advice — run the tool, never quote this — is what caught it. Recommended replacement: update to "218/221 static positives, negatives 208/208 (measured 2026-07-24 after #989's OSS validator-guard taint rules)", keeping the surrounding "run `validate-calibration`; never quote this number" wording verbatim.

## Follow-ups (not fixed here)

- `docs/gtm/10-old-docs-crosscheck.md` names the moved briefs while describing a crosscheck of `docs/` as it stood at the time. Left alone deliberately — rewriting the paths would falsify a historical record of what was in `docs/`.
- `docs/design/architecture.md` and `docs/design/epic-builder*.md` reference a `docs/briefs/` path for *target-repo* brief attachment, which is a different thing from Harvey's own `briefs/`. Left alone; not wrong, but easy to misread.
- A live crAPI re-run through `--mode=external` would convert the crAPI portability doc's status block from "covered by design + offline control" to measured. Worth an issue.
- `docs/design/spec-71-security-corpus.md` and `docs/runbooks/dry-run-calibration.md` still carry 2026-07-08-era corpus figures (17 positives + 15 negatives; the 0/8 historical baseline). Those read as dated historical records in context, so I did not restate them — but if they are being read as current, they need the same treatment carbon got.

`pnpm verify` green in the foreground: 172 test files, 3197 tests, typecheck/lint/knip clean. Several tests read docs from disk, so this is the meaningful gate for a docs change.

items.title: lua examples/probability_helpers.lua
items.body:
## Summary

This PR prepares LuaSF for `v0.7.0` by implementing lightweight probability and combinatorics helpers.

It builds on the modular source layout introduced in `v0.5.0` and the shape statistics helpers added in `v0.6.0`.

## What changed

### Implemented probability helpers

Implemented:

```text
src/luasf/probability.lua
```

The module adds:

```lua
stats.factorial(n)
stats.permutations(n, r)
stats.combinations(n, r)
stats.permutations_with_repetition(n, r)
stats.combinations_with_repetition(n, r)
stats.nPr(n, r)
stats.nCr(n, r)
```

### Combinatorics scope

This release makes the distinction between combinatorics without repetition and with repetition explicit:

```lua
stats.permutations(n, r)                 -- ordered selections without repetition
stats.combinations(n, r)                 -- unordered selections without repetition
stats.permutations_with_repetition(n, r) -- ordered selections with repetition
stats.combinations_with_repetition(n, r) -- unordered selections with repetition
```

Aliases were also added:

```lua
stats.nPr(n, r) -- alias for permutations(n, r)
stats.nCr(n, r) -- alias for combinations(n, r)
```

### Added tests

Added:

```text
spec/test_probability.lua
```

The tests cover:

* `factorial(n)`
* permutations without repetition
* combinations without repetition
* permutations with repetition
* combinations with repetition
* `nPr` and `nCr` aliases
* validation for invalid inputs

### Added example

Added:

```text
examples/probability_helpers.lua
```

The example demonstrates:

```lua
stats.factorial(5)
stats.permutations(5, 3)
stats.combinations(5, 3)
stats.permutations_with_repetition(5, 3)
stats.combinations_with_repetition(5, 3)
```

### Added LuaRocks rockspec

Added:

```text
rockspec/luasf-0.7.0-1.rockspec
```

The rockspec prepares LuaSF for the `v0.7.0` LuaRocks package release.

### Updated workflows

Updated GitHub Actions workflows to include the new probability helper test and example:

```bash
lua spec/test_probability.lua
lua examples/probability_helpers.lua
```

Updated files:

```text
.github/workflows/ci.yml
.github/workflows/publish-luarocks.yml
```

### Updated documentation

Updated documentation for the new helpers:

```text
README.md
docs/api.md
CHANGELOG.md
CONTRIBUTING.md
```

## Compatibility notes

This PR does not remove or rename existing public functions.

Existing usage remains supported:

```lua
local stats = require("luasf")
local stats = require("LuaSF")
local stats = require("LuaStat")
```

Legacy function names remain available.

## Numeric precision note

Probability helpers use Lua numbers. Very large inputs may exceed the practical numeric precision or range of the Lua runtime.

Arbitrary-precision arithmetic is intentionally not included in this release to keep LuaSF small, pure-Lua, and dependency-light.

## Testing

Test locally with:

```bash
lua spec/test_stats.lua
lua spec/test_distributions.lua
lua spec/test_sampling.lua
lua spec/test_bivariate.lua
lua spec/test_shape.lua
lua spec/test_probability.lua
```

Examples can be run with:

```bash
lua examples/dice_simulation.lua
lua examples/normal_quality_control.lua
lua examples/gamma_distribution.lua
lua examples/weighted_loot_drop.lua
lua examples/monte_carlo_pi.lua
lua examples/poisson_arrivals.lua
lua examples/binomial_coin_flips.lua
lua examples/bootstrap_mean.lua
lua examples/covariance_correlation.lua
lua examples/skewness_kurtosis.lua
lua examples/probability_helpers.lua
```

## Release target

This PR prepares LuaSF for:

```text
v0.7.0 - Probability Helpers
```

## Scope note

LuaSF remains focused on lightweight statistics, probability helpers, random variables, sampling, and simulation utilities.

Optimization-based modeling, machine learning workflows, model training pipelines, and non-linear regression remain outside the current scope of LuaSF.

items.title: feat: privacy mode — checksum-validated PII redaction with stable pseudonyms
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds **privacy mode**: opt-in redaction of personal identifiers — TCKN, VKN, IBAN, payment card, IMEI, email, phone — from command output and from the command lines written to the audit and policy logs. Detection is checksum-based rather than machine learning, and each match is replaced by a stable HMAC-derived pseudonym the agent can still correlate on.

Enable with `[privacy] enabled`, `vallum run --privacy`, or `VALLUM_PRIVACY=1`. Default off.

```
musteri,tckn,telefon
Ali,[TCKN_3f9be1ac],[PHONE_2d38cc58]
Ayse,[TCKN_c7789072],[PHONE_e5847f0d]
Ali,[TCKN_3f9be1ac],[PHONE_2d38cc58]     ← same person, same aliases
```

The agent can count distinct records, join two outputs, or spot a repeated row — without ever seeing a real value. Aliases are `HMAC-SHA256(machine secret, category || value)`, derived rather than stored, so they stay stable across commands and sessions with **zero personal data at rest**.

### Why no model

The prompt for this work was `openai/privacy-filter`. It is not used, and nothing is trained. Every category here has a checksum, and a checksum returns an answer where a classifier returns a probability. Vallum is also a single static binary on the hot path of every command an agent runs — any inference runtime means a multi-hundred-MB artifact and a resident daemon. The categories where a model genuinely wins — free-text person names, addresses, dates — are explicitly out of scope.

### Design decision worth reviewing

Checksums alone are **not** enough. Roughly 1 in 100 random 11-digit runs satisfies the TCKN equations, and ordinary output is full of numbers. The precision corpus proved it: `Content-Length: 12345678950` and `worker=12345678950` both carry checksum-valid TCKNs, `Total: 1234567890` a valid VKN, and `processed 4111111111111111 records` a Luhn-valid Visa-prefixed run. These are byte-for-byte indistinguishable from `kimlik no 12345678950` by any positional rule.

So an identifier-ish **key name is required** for the weak-checksum categories:

| Category | Key name required | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `tckn`, `vkn`, `card`, `imei` | yes | residual false-accept rate too high to stand alone |
| `iban` | no | mod-97 *and* per-country length behind a distinctive prefix |
| `email` | no | unmistakable shape |
| `phone` | no | only matched behind an explicit `+` dial code or `0`+`5XX` block |

A negative key list (`content-length`, `size`, `total`, …) was considered and rejected as inherently incomplete — `Retry-After:` and `chunk_id=` are in the benign corpus specifically to hold that line.

Context comes from an assignment/JSON key within 40 bytes on the same line, **or** a delimited-table column whose header names one. The column path matters: a byte-distance lookback reaches a CSV header from row 1 only, which redacts the first record and silently leaks every row below it.

**Accepted cost:** a bare value with no key name near it is not redacted. This bites when a pipeline drops the header — `grep Ali customers.csv` loses the `tckn` column name, so that column stays visible while its `email` and `phone` columns are still redacted. Documented under Known limits.

### Also included

`scrubber::sanitize` / `redact` now take a `ScrubOptions` struct instead of positional booleans (**breaking** for library consumers). They already carried three bools across 18 call sites; a fourth would have produced `sanitize(x, &e, false, true, true, true)` at every caller.

A `[privacy]` table in a project-level `.vallum.toml` is rejected, so a checked-in file cannot switch the mode off — already structural via `deny_unknown_fields`, now locked in by test.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --all` — 878 passing, 0 failures
- [x] `cargo test --all --features bpe`
- [x] User-facing changes noted in `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`
- [x] Docs updated where behavior changed (README, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/architecture.md`)

**Detection changes:**

- [x] Corpus/regression entries added — `evals/corpus/pii.jsonl` (positives) and `evals/corpus/pii_benign.jsonl` (the precision gate, incl. adversarial checksum-valid lines); eval floors still pass
- [x] Test fixtures are synthetic — every TCKN/VKN/IBAN/card value is derived from the algorithm under test or is a published test vector. No real personal data enters the repo, and no secret-shaped fixtures were added.

New test files: `tests/pii_precision.rs` (primary gate, sibling of `policy_precision.rs`), `tests/pii_redaction.rs`, `tests/pii_zero_impact.rs`.

## Anything reviewers should focus on?

1. **The key-context requirement is the load-bearing decision.** It is what makes the mode usable on real output, and it is also the recall cost. If you disagree with where the line falls between context-free and context-required categories, that is the thing to argue about — it lives in one place, `Category::requires_key_context`.

2. **`gate.rs` is where the precision lives.** `detect_header` requires a following row of matching shape before treating a line as a header, the lookback is clamped to its own line, and short vocabulary entries (`tel`, `vkn`, `cep`) must land on a word boundary so `telemetry_id=` does not read as a phone key. Each of those three came from a test failure, not foresight — worth a second look for cases I did not hit.

3. **VKN algorithm.** Cross-checked against an independent reference; the special-case forms differ but are provably equivalent (noted in the doc comment). Note that the same reference's *TCKN* function is buggy — `substr(9, 0)` returns an empty string — so TCKN was validated against a published test vector instead, not that reference.

4. **Zero-impact claim.** `tests/pii_zero_impact.rs` asserts that with the mode off the existing benign corpus, and even all-PII text, pass through byte-identical. Worth confirming that is the guarantee you want from an opt-in security feature.

items.title: Release v4.11.0
items.body:
## New Features

### Change

1. **Multi-sig is now a first-class workflow in the TypeScript CLI.** `permission show` and `permission update` read and replace an account's permission structure on chain (the latter burns 100 TRX and warns before an owner lockout); every broadcast command gained `--permission-id <n>`, `--expiration <ms>`, and a new `--build-only` early-exit mode alongside `--dry-run` / `--sign-only`. `tx sign` now takes a transaction hex via `--hex` / `--file`, appends exactly one signature while preserving prior ones, and reports how far the accumulated weight is from the threshold — refusing before a key is ever decrypted if the account is not in the permission group (`not_authorized`) or has already approved (`already_signed`); `--offline` keeps the air-gapped path. `tx approvals` is the read-only companion that shows the permission group, threshold, accumulated weight, approved signers, and expiration without signing. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

2. **`tx multisig` adds optional collaboration through the TronLink multi-sig service.** Where the on-chain path passes a hex from person to person, the service holds the transaction, accumulates signatures, and pushes notifications: the default mode lists transactions awaiting this account, `--create` signs an unsigned hex and opens a collection at `1 / N`, `--sign <txId>` co-signs a pending one, and `--watch` keeps a WebSocket open and reports only the count awaiting your signature (never transaction content). Once the threshold is reached the service broadcasts. Credentials (`tronlinkSecretId` / `tronlinkSecretKey` / `tronlinkChannel`) are set with `config` and are per-environment; without them the command fails with `tronlink_credentials_missing`. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

3. **`gasfree` brings gas-less token transfers to the TypeScript CLI.** `gasfree info` reports your GasFree address, activation status, nonce, and fee schedule; `gasfree transfer` signs an EIP-712 structured-data transfer and submits it to the GasFree provider, which puts it on chain and charges the fee in the transferred token itself, so no TRX is required; `gasfree trace <traceId>` follows the provider's `WAITING → INPROGRESS → CONFIRMING → SUCCEED / FAILED` states. Because submission goes to a provider rather than a node, the receipt carries a `traceId` instead of a `txId` — follow it with `--wait` or `gasfree trace`, not `tx status`. Credentials are `gasfreeApiKey` / `gasfreeApiSecret` via `config`. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

4. **New account-lifecycle and local-utility commands.** `account activate` creates a not-yet-existing address on chain without transferring any asset, with the payer covering the creation fee; `account set` writes the on-chain name or account id (permanent on mainnet, so it is deliberately one-at-a-time). A local contact book — `contact add` / `list` / `remove`, stored `0600` in the config directory — lets a saved name be used wherever a recipient is expected (`tx send --to`, `gasfree transfer --to`). `encoding convert <input>` auto-detects an input and prints every equivalent representation (TRON base58 / TRON hex / EVM / public key, or hex / Base64 / Base58Check), rejecting secrets outright. `address generate` produces a throwaway keypair offline, writing the private key to a `0600` file rather than the terminal unless `--print-secret` is passed. `current --qr` renders a scannable receive-address QR in text mode without unlocking or touching the network. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

5. **The Java documentation was split out of `java/README.md` into a browsable `java/docs/` tree.** The README shrank from a single ~2,700-line page to an overview with quick links; commands now live under `docs/commands/` by domain (wallet, account, transfers, staking, multisig, GasFree, DEX, proposals, contracts, …), with `docs/concepts/`, `docs/guide/`, and a field-by-field `docs/reference/config.md`. Stale planning and QA scratch documents were removed. No Java behavior changed in this release apart from the version constant. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

## Bug Fixes

### Change

1. **A transaction the node rejected could be reported as submitted.** TronWeb does not throw on rejection — it hands back the node's response verbatim, and a rejected `/wallet/broadcasttransaction` carries no `result` field at all, so the previous `result === false` check never fired and the CLI returned a success envelope with a txId for a transaction that was never accepted. Acceptance is now white-listed (`result !== true` is a rejection) on both the object and `--hex` broadcast paths, surfacing the node's reason as `transaction_rejected`. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

2. **`block` lost precision on large int64 fields.** Block responses were parsed through JavaScript numbers, so protobuf int64/uint64 values beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` came back rounded. Blocks are now fetched and parsed losslessly, with out-of-range integers preserved as exact decimal strings. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

3. **`--dry-run` reported doomed staking requests as fine.** `stake freeze` and `stake unfreeze` are rejected by the node at broadcast time when the amount exceeds the available balance or the amount actually staked for that resource, but `--dry-run` never reaches the node — so a request that could not possibly succeed previewed cleanly. Both now pre-flight against the chain and fail with `insufficient_balance` / `insufficient_stake`. Relatedly, `contract send` now warns when the supplied `--fee-limit` is below the energy estimate at the current energy price, and the staked-amount computation was corrected for the node's habit of omitting the default `BANDWIDTH` enum in `frozenV2`. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

4. **Chain-controlled text could repaint the terminal.** Permission names, token names and symbols, and co-signer labels are written by whoever put them on chain. Terminal control bytes were already stripped, but bidirectional and zero-width formatting characters passed straight through — `U+202E` reverses the display order of everything after it, letting a crafted name change how the address or weight beside it appears, and zero-width characters can make two different names render identically. Text mode now escapes them visibly (`<U+202E>`) rather than dropping them, so legitimate right-to-left text still displays normally and tampering is obvious. JSON output is never rewritten. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

5. **Filesystem failures surfaced as raw OS errors.** `backup` and the atomic config/keystore writers let Node `ErrnoException`s escape, producing `internal_error` and, on a failed write, leaving a truncated or empty file at the destination. Failures are now typed as `io_error` with the partial artifact removed, and the multi-file atomic write reports a rolled-back failure distinctly from one that committed but could not confirm durability. Two new config-file conditions are also reported explicitly: `invalid_config` when `config.yaml` cannot be parsed (the parser detail is withheld, since it quotes the offending line and may carry a credential) and `insecure_config` when the file holds service credentials but is a symlink or group/world-readable. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

6. **Positional arguments rejected number-shaped values.** Yargs inferred a type for the anonymous positional tail, so a value such as `0xdeadbeef` or `12345` arrived at its string-typed field as a number and was rejected. The tail is now typed as strings so the raw token survives parsing. As a consequence, a field exposed as a positional no longer also accepts its `--<field>` spelling — this affects the undocumented `config --key/--value` and `block --number` forms; the documented positional form is unchanged, and the global `--account` flag still works on `use` / `rename` / `delete` / `backup`. ([#963](https://github.com/tronprotocol/wallet-cli/pull/963))

items.title: Test-suite and delivery hardening: strict traces, netstandard2.1 API baseline, analyzers as errors
items.body:
## What this does

**Test-suite hardening.** The three order-insensitive assertions on observer traces are now sequence-exact (all stayed green — the traces were already correct, the assertions were weaker than the contract). Wall-clock upper bounds are removed or widened with lower bounds kept, every unbounded-delay await gained a `[CancelAfter]` hang guard or a bounded delay, dead unreachable `CancelAsync` calls are gone, and Linear/Exponential retry backoff is now exercised end-to-end (lower-bound-only asserts; a fake-clock seam was considered and rejected — recorded in the fixture). The AllocationGate pins JIT tiering for determinism, folds four inline measure loops into the shared helpers, and gains nine cases (Switch dispatch, non-blackboard Choice, async token any-merge/retry/scratch, sync token observer, async timeout wrapper). `NxGraph.Serialization.Tests` converges on the NUnit 4 line, the last shared mutable static in the suite is gone, and sync Switch and async token pool/multiplicity coverage twins are added.

**A netstandard2.1 public-API baseline** (MetadataLoadContext walk over the built dll against the NETStandard.Library.Ref facades, `NxGraph.netstandard2.1.approved.txt`, same `NXGRAPH_UPDATE_PUBLIC_API=1` mechanism, skip-with-message on partial builds). It immediately caught a real finding: the `System.ArgumentNullExceptionShim` polyfill ships **public** in the netstandard2.1 (Unity-facing) build — now pinned by the baseline; internalizing it is a deliberate follow-up surface change.

**Delivery hardening.** A root `Directory.Build.props` centralizes language/analyzer/metadata props with .NET analyzers at `latest-recommended` and `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` across all eight projects (all pre-existing warnings fixed; every `NoWarn` carries an in-file justification; `NxGraph.Build`'s props import the root so its `.tools/` isolation is preserved; SourceLink/determinism gate on CI env vars). The coverage gate runs on the single coverlet.msbuild driver — proven live: `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=99` fails ci with the threshold error, default 70 passes with NxGraph at 80.93% line coverage; the CI artifact now uploads the same driver's lcov output. `NUGET_API_KEY` is no longer echoed on local publishes (redacted command line, including in failure text). Workflow actions are SHA-pinned with tag comments (checkout v4.3.1, setup-dotnet v4.3.1, upload-artifact v4.6.2, action-gh-release v2.6.2), the dispatch help lists all targets, and `REPO_BRANCH` is correct on tag builds. The committed UPM manifest now carries the last released version (2.1.0-alpha) with the policy recorded in the release checklist.

**Benchmark refresh.** Fairness fixes in the Stateless comparison (no `IterationSetup` on ns-scale ops, honest timeout analog, CSV exporter parity), sync Timeout/Director twins, and 14 new feature benchmarks (parallel round, dynamic selection, blackboard typed-key vs dictionary, token diamond, port relay, suspend/resume, Switch). The README table and chart are re-measured (ShortRun, 2026-07-19) on the combined tree of the open hardening PRs, so the published numbers describe main after they all land; a higher-precision A/B of the sync single node against pre-change main measured +2.4 ns (51.5 vs 49.1 ns), the expected cost of the per-visit report-slot hygiene introduced by the log-bridge PR, with longer chains inside noise.

## Verification

`dotnet build -c Release` fully clean under warnings-as-errors; 653 + 193 tests green at the branch tip; `dotnet run --project NxGraph.Build -- ci` green end-to-end at the default threshold and with `CI=true` (determinism props + baselines healthy together).

## Merge notes

**Land this PR last.** After the other three hardening PRs merge, update this branch from main — the combination was validated locally (full suite and ci green under warnings-as-errors on the merged tree; expected clean auto-merge, no conflicting regions).
