### [`v3.20.3`](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.20.3): Protocol Buffers v3.20.3

### Java

- Refactoring java full runtime to reuse sub-message builders and prepare to
  migrate parsing logic from parse constructor to builder.
- Move proto wireformat parsing functionality from the private "parsing
  constructor" to the Builder class.
- Change the Lite runtime to prefer merging from the wireformat into mutable
  messages rather than building up a new immutable object before merging. This
  way results in fewer allocations and copy operations.
- Make message-type extensions merge from wire-format instead of building up
  instances and merging afterwards. This has much better performance.
- Fix TextFormat parser to build up recurring (but supposedly not repeated)
  sub-messages directly from text rather than building a new sub-message and
  merging the fully formed message into the existing field.
- This release addresses a [Security Advisory for Java users](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-h4h5-3hr4-j3g2)

### [`v3.20.2`](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.20.2): Protocol Buffers v3.20.2

### C++

- Reduce memory consumption of MessageSet parsing
- This release addresses a [Security Advisory for C++ and Python users](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-8gq9-2x98-w8hf)

### [`v3.20.1`](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.20.1): Protocol Buffers v3.20.1

### PHP

- Fix building packaged PHP extension ([#​9727](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9727))
- Fixed composer.json to only advertise compatibility with PHP 7.0+.  ([#​9819](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9819))

### Ruby

- Disable the aarch64 build on macOS until it can be fixed. ([#​9816](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9816))

### Other

- Fix versioning issues in 3.20.0

### [`v3.20.0`](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.20.0): Protocol Buffers v3.20.0

2022-03-25 version 3.20.0 (C++/Java/Python/PHP/Objective-C/C#/Ruby/JavaScript)

### Ruby

- Dropped Ruby 2.3 and 2.4 support for CI and releases. ([#​9311](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9311))
- Added Ruby 3.1 support for CI and releases ([#​9566](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9566)).
- Message.decode/encode: Add recursion\_limit option ([#​9218](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9218)/[#​9486](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9486))
- Allocate with xrealloc()/xfree() so message allocation is visible to the
  Ruby GC.  In certain tests this leads to much lower memory usage due to more
  frequent GC runs ([#​9586](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9586)).
- Fix conversion of singleton classes in Ruby ([#​9342](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9342))
- Suppress warning for intentional circular require ([#​9556](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9556))
- JSON will now output shorter strings for double and float fields when possible
  without losing precision.
- Encoding and decoding of binary format will now work properly on big-endian
  systems.
- UTF-8 verification was fixed to properly reject surrogate code points.
- Unknown enums for proto2 protos now properly implement proto2's behavior of
  putting such values in unknown fields.

### Java

- Revert "Standardize on Array copyOf" ([#​9400](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9400))
- Resolve more java field accessor name conflicts ([#​8198](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/8198))
- Don't support map fields in DynamicMessage.Builder.{getFieldBuilder,getRepeatedFieldBuilder}
- Fix parseFrom to only throw InvalidProtocolBufferException
- InvalidProtocolBufferException now allows arbitrary wrapped Exception types.
- Fix bug in `FieldSet.Builder.mergeFrom`
- Flush CodedOutputStream also flushes underlying OutputStream
- When oneof case is the same and the field type is Message, merge the
  subfield. (previously it was replaced.)’
- Add [@​CheckReturnValue](https://redirect.github.com/CheckReturnValue) to some protobuf types
- Report original exceptions when parsing JSON
- Add more info to [@​deprecated](https://redirect.github.com/deprecated) javadoc for set/get/has methods
- Fix initialization bug in doc comment line numbers
- Fix comments for message set wire format.

### Kotlin

- Add test scope to kotlin-test for protobuf-kotlin-lite ([#​9518](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9518))
- Add orNull extensions for optional message fields.
- Add orNull extensions to all proto3 message fields.

### Python

- Dropped support for Python < 3.7 ([#​9480](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9480))
- Protoc is now able to generate python stubs (.pyi) with --pyi\_out
- Pin multibuild scripts to get manylinux1 wheels back ([#​9216](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9216))
- Fix type annotations of some Duration and Timestamp methods.
- Repeated field containers are now generic in field types and could be used
  in type annotations.
  \*\[Breaking change] Protobuf python generated codes are simplified. Descriptors and message
  classes' definitions are now dynamic created in internal/builder.py.
  Insertion Points for messages classes are discarded.
- has\_presence is added for FieldDescriptor in python
- Loosen indexing type requirements to allow valid **index**() implementations
  rather than only PyLongObjects.
- Fix the deepcopy bug caused by not copying message\_listener.
- Added python JSON parse recursion limit (default 100)
- Path info is added for python JSON parse errors
- Pure python repeated scalar fields will not able to pickle. Convert to list
  first.
- Timestamp.ToDatetime() now accepts an optional tzinfo parameter. If
  specified, the function returns a timezone-aware datetime in the given time
  zone. If omitted or None, the function returns a timezone-naive UTC datetime
  (as previously).
- Adds client\_streaming and server\_streaming fields to MethodDescriptor.
- Add "ensure\_ascii" parameter to json\_format.MessageToJson. This allows smaller
  JSON serializations with UTF-8 or other non-ASCII encodings.
- Added experimental support for directly assigning numpy scalars and array.
- Improve the calculation of public\_dependencies in DescriptorPool.
- \[Breaking Change] Disallow setting fields to numpy singleton arrays or repeated fields to numpy

items.title: Unify the RNG, address simulation randomness by label, and target precision instead of iterations
items.body:
## What this is

The 5 → 1 → 2 chain from the ideation, in 16 commits: unify the RNG, address the
simulator's randomness by label so common random numbers work, and let a forecast target a
precision instead of an iteration count.

## Verification

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace` | 293 passed | **311 passed** |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` | clean | clean |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean | clean |
| `cargo build --workspace --release` | ok | ok |

`1529 insertions(+) / 221 deletions(-)` across 15 files. Every commit is independently green.

## Phase 5 — one generator (commits 1-8)

`oracle-numeric` gains `range`, `int_inclusive`, `chance`, a Marsaglia-Tsang `gamma`, and
`Rng::stream` for labelled substreams. `oracle-sim` and `oracle-ingest` then come off
`rand`/`rand_distr` entirely.

Being precise about what the dependency removal achieves: **`rand_distr` is gone from
`Cargo.lock` outright**. `rand` is no longer ours but stays transitively (tungstenite →
axum → oracle-api), so the build graph barely shrinks. What it does buy is that the
workspace's randomness is single-sourced — "reproducible from the seed" is now a property
of the whole pipeline rather than of each crate separately, which is the actual
prerequisite for the CRN work.

The `gamma` sampler is validated three ways rather than on moments alone, since matching a
mean and variance is weak evidence for a *shape*: moments across shapes either side of 1,
the exponential tail identity at shape 1 (`P(X > θ) = 1/e`), and the composed mixture's
variance against the analytic negative-binomial `mean + mean²/size`.

## Phase 1 — common random numbers (commits 9-13)

Every draw is now addressed by what it belongs to: team strength by team index, group
fixtures by `MatchId`, knockout ties by `(round, slot)`.

The two identity choices are opposite on purpose. A group fixture keys on its **match id**,
because keying on list position would break the moment a scenario removes some *other*
fixture and renumbered the rest. A knockout tie keys on its **bracket position**, because
who reaches a quarter-final is exactly what a scenario changes — keying on the pairing
would hand the tie fresh randomness whenever the scenario altered who got there.

**Measured result: ~6x.** Conditioning one group result leaves the other eleven groups'
qualification probabilities drifting ~0.0017 instead of ~0.0100, consistently across seeds.

**Measured non-result, which changed the plan.** This buys *nothing* for the
champion-probability swings `kingmaker` reports — 8 seeds gave a coupled swing SD of 0.0078
against 0.0062 uncoupled. The cause is structural, not a defect: conditioning the match
changes how often the team tops its group, so it enters a different bracket slot and its
knockout path is legitimately different randomness. That path change *is* the causal effect
being measured, so no keying can couple it away.

I originally pitched this as reducing swing noise. It does not, and the commit history says
so where it was discovered rather than quietly moving on. Which redirected the second half
of the work to what actually helps: if the swing carries irreducible noise, report it with
its uncertainty. Each swing is now a `PairedDifference` — mean, standard error, iteration
count — computed from per-iteration differences, the only correct method when the runs are
correlated, plus `is_significant()` for the question a reader actually has.

## Phase 2 — precision targeting (commits 14-16)

`--precision 0.002` / `?precision=0.002` replaces guessing an iteration count; `--iters`
becomes the ceiling. Verified end to end:

```
--iters 20000                      20000 iters, ±0.2% per-team error
--precision 0.004                  10000 iters, "target reached ... ±0.0030"
--precision 0.0015                 45000 iters, "target reached ... ±0.0014"
--precision 0.0001 --iters 6000     6000 iters, "target NOT reached: stopped at the
                                    6000-iteration ceiling ... ±0.0040"
```

**A real statistical bug this surfaced.** The natural stopping statistic
`sqrt(p(1-p)/N)` is exactly **zero** for a team that has not yet won an iteration — and
most of a 48-team field never does, so a run could halt claiming perfect precision. My
degenerate-input test caught it at N=1, where every team's share is 0 or 1 and the run
stopped after a single iteration reporting the target met. Fixed with Agresti-Coull "plus
four" shrinkage, so never having observed an event is no longer confused with knowing it
cannot happen. Two tests pin it.

## Things worth a reviewer's attention

**Batching must be transparent.** A precision run assembled from batches is asserted
bit-identical to one straight run of the same length (`0..1500` + `1500..4000` vs
`0..4000`). Without that, extending a run would silently rerandomise what it already had.

**`champion_indicators` is checked to average to exactly the aggregate `p_champion`** (to
1e-12), so the paired series provably measures the same quantity as the ordinary forecast.

**Two caveats documented rather than buried:** stopping on an observed error is a sequential
decision and so mildly optimistic; and a target near zero is unreachable at any finite cost.

**Synthetic numbers moved, and none of it is a model improvement.** Commit 6 changes every
synthetic value, so README's synthetic backtest table is updated. The ensemble now edges the
synthetic market where it previously trailed, and ECE reads 0.011 against 0.030 — that is a
different dataset, not a better model, and I added a README note saying so because a reader
would otherwise be invited to the flattering conclusion. `docs/VALIDATION.md`'s real-data
numbers are untouched: that path goes through `load_results_csv` and calls none of the
migrated generators, checked by inspection.

**One test bug found by an end-to-end check**, worth mentioning because it shows the check
works: asserting two seeds agree within 3σ initially failed on row *ordering* — rows are
ranked by swing magnitude, so seeds can order them differently and they must be paired by
fixture.

**A stale doc claim corrected:** ARCHITECTURE said `oracle-players` carried its own
SplitMix64 "so it carries no `rand` dependency". Both halves are now false.

## Note on the base

Branches off `main` (PR #2 merged). Targets `main`.

items.title: B3: Compat-sensitive infra — opt-in bearer auth, CockroachDB big-int IDs, DB schema selection (#48, #69, #78)
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Third backlog batch: the compat-sensitive infrastructure issues. Every change is opt-in or additive, so the default deployment behaves exactly as before.

- **#48 — Opt-in bearer-token auth.** New `spoolman/auth.py` pure-ASGI middleware, registered on the v1 sub-app **only when `SPOOLMAN_API_TOKEN` is set**. It guards HTTP requests and the websocket handshake (WS takes the token as `?token=` since browsers can't set headers), while leaving `GET /health`, the OpenAPI docs, `/metrics`, and the SPA open. `request.state.principal` is stamped so #52's accounts layer on without rework. The client stores the token in localStorage and attaches it to axios/`apiFetch`/the WS URL; a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` 401 opens a token-entry modal (kept distinct from the #47 forward-auth-proxy reload path). Unset ⇒ no middleware ⇒ current behaviour.
- **#69 — CockroachDB big-int IDs.** `unique_rowid()` exceeds JS `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so `JSON.parse` rounded ids and the UI 404'd. The client now parses responses with `json-bigint` (`storeAsString`), keeping only precision-losing integers as strings and leaving normal serial ids as numbers — behaviour changes only for oversized ids, and the server is untouched. Wired into the axios `transformResponse` and the websocket message parse.
- **#78 — `SPOOLMAN_DB_SCHEMA`.** Optional Postgres/CockroachDB schema (search_path) for shared databases (e.g. Supabase); the schema is created and migrated into automatically. `Database.connect()` is shared by the app and Alembic, so both pick it up. MySQL/SQLite have no schemas → logged and ignored. The postgres integration compose now runs against a non-default schema for CI coverage.

## Checklist

- [x] Behavioral tests added/updated — `tests/test_auth.py` (on/off matrix, open routes, WS handshake, principal), `tests/test_db_schema.py`, `get_api_token`/`get_db_schema` cases in `tests/test_env.py`, and client `apiToken`/`bigintJson`/`authReloadHandler` (Bearer-401 + token-header) tests. Green: 368 backend + 437 client.
- [x] New or changed UI strings added to `client/public/locales/en/common.json` — `apiToken.*`.
- [x] API changes stay under `/api/v1` and remain backward compatible — auth is opt-in (default off = today's behaviour, Moonraker/OctoPrint can send the header); the big-int fix is client-only and never changes server serialization; `SPOOLMAN_DB_SCHEMA` is opt-in and Postgres/CRDB-only.
- [x] Schema changes come with a linear Alembic migration — n/a, no table changes; `migrations/env.py` only gains schema-aware config.

Docs: README "Security & exposure", `SECURITY.md`, `docs/installation.md`, `.env.example`.

items.title: refactor(relationships,reducer): centralize correlation confidence into documented registries
items.body:
Closes #3490

## What

Correlation confidence values were hand-tuned magic constants scattered as inline `float64` literals across ~15 `relationships` extractor files and the `reducer` candidate loader, with no central provenance, no documented rationale per value, and no test guarding their relative ordering. The Bayesian corroboration math in `resolver.go` was principled; its inputs were not auditable or calibratable.

This centralizes both confidence taxonomies into single, documented, overridable registries and pins the confidence semantics with invariant tests:

- **`go/internal/relationships/confidence.go`** — `DefaultConfidenceRegistry`, keyed by `EvidenceKind`, each entry carrying a value, a `ConfidenceTier`, and a rationale. Named family accessors cover the runtime-service and schema-driven Terraform extractors whose `EvidenceKind` strings are computed at runtime.
- **`go/internal/reducer/workload_signal_confidence.go`** — `DefaultWorkloadSignalConfidence`, keyed by `WorkloadSignalKind`, each entry carrying a value, a `WorkloadSignalTier`, and a rationale.

Both registries are immutable after construction and expose `WithOverrides(...)` for calibration without editing source or mutating the shared default. All extractors and the candidate loader now read their priors from the registries instead of inline literals.

## Why this is safe (no correlation-truth change)

Every emitted confidence value is **byte-identical** to the prior inline literal (registries are built once at package init and read by O(1) map lookup; provenance kind strings are unchanged). This is a pure structural refactor — no evidence, candidate, resolved-relationship, or workload-admission behavior changes.

## Invariants pinned (written failing-first, TDD)

- every `EvidenceKind` / `WorkloadSignalKind` has a documented registry entry (a new kind without one fails the build)
- every value is within `[0,1]`
- tier floors are strictly monotonic; each registered value respects its declared tier floor
- **ordering / monotonicity**: direct-binding > strong-reference > reference > weak-reference; and on the reducer side, runtime signals strictly outrank CI/controller provenance
- the calibration override hook validates bounds and never mutates the default
- the schema-driven resource-name fallback weight stays below `DefaultConfidenceThreshold`

## Follow-up

Full statistical calibration (golden-set precision/recall per evidence kind to re-derive the absolute numbers, and justify the 0.75 threshold from the curve) remains future work. These registries are the structural prerequisite: the numbers now live in one auditable, overridable place instead of scattered literals.

## Evidence

- `cd go && go test ./internal/relationships ./internal/reducer -count=1` → 2406 pass (incl. unchanged `resolver_confidence_test.go`, `evidence_test.go`, `candidate_loader_test.go`)
- `cd go && go test ./internal/query ./internal/mcp ./cmd/reducer ./cmd/ingester -count=1` → 4033 pass
- new focused tests: `go test ./... -run 'Confidence|WorkloadSignal'` → all pass
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/relationships/... ./internal/reducer/...` → 0 issues
- `scripts/verify-package-docs.sh`, `scripts/verify-performance-evidence.sh` → pass
- `git diff --check` → clean
- docs updated: `relationships` README + AGENTS, `reducer` README (registry model, tier tables, No-Regression / No-Observability-Change markers)

items.title: feat(lynx-sqlite): embedded SQLite database module with migrations and live queries
items.body:
Closes #466. Adds `@sigx/lynx-sqlite` — an embedded SQLite database module, the persistence layer for chat-style offline-first apps (message history, conversations, local caches).

**What's in it**

- **Core API** (`openDatabase` / `execute` / `executeBatch` / `transaction()` / `close` / `deleteDatabase`): async-only (statements run on a per-database native executor, the BG JS thread is never blocked), positional `?` binding with JS-side coercion (boolean→1/0, undefined→NULL, BLOBs rejected with guidance), `{ error }` callback convention matching the other modules.
- **Transactions**: a JS-side operation queue per database serializes `execute`/`executeBatch`/`transaction` so an open transaction is never interleaved with foreign statements (Promises don't cross the bridge; native runs one statement at a time per handle).
- **Migrations**: ordered `PRAGMA user_version` migrations, each atomic with its version bump (crash-safe resume).
- **`useLiveQuery` hook**: re-runs a query whenever one of its tables is written through this API. Invalidation is JS-side (conservative table extraction from the SQL, `'*'` fallback when uncertain; transaction notifications fire once, on commit) — no native update hooks, ports verbatim to a future web backend.
- **Native**: Android via framework `android.database.sqlite` (typed binds incl. a CursorFactory for queries, WAL on open, per-handle single-thread executor in a process-wide store); iOS via system `libsqlite3` (prepare/bind/step, WAL, serial queue per handle, files under `Library/Application Support/SQLite/`). No bundled C library, no pods, no Gradle deps.
- **Showcase**: a WhatsApp-style chat thread demo (migrate → seed → live-query list → simulated incoming replies via timer writes).
- 45 new vitest tests (mocked bridge): param coercion, error unwrapping, transaction serialization order, commit-only change notifications, migration semantics, table-extractor corpus, hook lifecycle.

**Design notes / defaults** (flagged for review)

- iOS DB location is `Library/Application Support/SQLite/` (not iCloud-backed Documents — chat history can be large).
- INTEGER columns come back as JS numbers; >2^53 loses precision (documented: use TEXT ids).
- v2 candidates noted in README/issue: web backend (`@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` + OPFS), SQLCipher, FTS5 guidance, BLOB via base64, Drizzle driver adapter.

**Verification**: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (1861 passed), `pnpm lint` (only pre-existing warnings), `pnpm version:check` (52 packages at 0.6.1) all green. On-device showcase run pending reviewer feedback.

items.title: Agent eval harness, >90% coverage, and Z80 SingleStepTests/ZEXDOC conformance (6 core fixes)
items.body:
Three pieces of work, smallest blast radius first.

## 1. Agent eval harness — the headline roadmap milestone (`cell-eval/`)
Measures the actual thesis: *does an agent retrieve and run the right cell instead of writing code?* Two numbers that fail for different reasons:
- **retrieval precision** — deterministic, no model; paraphrase/adversarial dataset → P@1 / hit@k / MRR. Baseline: direct **1.00**, paraphrase **0.53**, adversarial **0.50** (token-overlap brittleness — the case for the type-led index).
- **adoption** — an LLM agent loop over an **OpenAI-compatible / Ollama** endpoint; cell tools as function calls. Baseline (gemma-4-26B): adoption **0.75**, correct **1.00**. Steering is a single held-fixed constant so library vs prompt changes don't get conflated.

Drives the same `CellLibrary` the MCP server exposes; adoption path gated, no network in CI.

## 2. Test coverage > 90% per file
- **Python** (cell-eval + cell80-mcp): 63% → **99%** — CLI, report renderers, dataset/library edges, the adoption agent loop via a fake OpenAI client, and the MCP tool bodies/entry point.
- **Rust** workspace: 89% → **96%** lines — `flags.rs`/`bus.rs` 0%→100%, `decode.rs` 64%→96% (opcode sweep), `cpu.rs` 80%→96% (control-flow tests), the CLI shim 0%→100%. Fixed a strict-doc broken intra-doc link.

## 3. Z80 SingleStepTests + ZEXDOC conformance — and six real core bugs
New per-opcode correctness harness (`z80-tests/`, data fetched on demand + git-ignored, skips cleanly when absent). Building it took the core from 44,514/72,000 → **1,530,000 / 1,530,000** across the full instruction set (base/CB/ED/DD/FD/DDCB/FDCB, incl. cycle counts and undocumented flags); **ZEXDOC** passes with no CRC mismatch. Six core bugs found and fixed:
- **EI/IFF**: sets IFF1/IFF2 immediately (only interrupt *accept* is delayed) — was breaking `EI; LD A,I`.
- **LDIR/LDDR, CPIR/CPDR**: repeat-iteration XY flags from PCh, not `A±(HL)` (Patrik Rak).
- **INIR/INDR/OTIR/OTDR**: repeat fixup for `wz`, XY, and H/P.
- **DD/FD-prefixed SCF/CCF**: the ineffective prefix re-latches Q (`q_prev` → 0).
- **LD (IX+d),n timing**: 19 T-states, not 22.

## Validation
- All workspace + Python test suites green; clippy `-D warnings` clean across all crates; docs build with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`.
- Docs/roadmap/README updated to reflect the eval harness and conformance results.

items.title: docs: add ARCHITECTURE.md + polish README for review
items.body:
## Summary

Operator-facing docs polish — the README is the first thing a  reads, restructured to make the review path explicit. NEW `ARCHITECTURE.md` is the 5-minute version of `docs/DESIGN.md` for time-pressed .

## Changes

### `README.md`

- New **"Reviewing this "** section near the top — points at `ARCHITECTURE.md` (5-minute path) → `docs/DESIGN.md` (15-minute path) — and gives a ready-made bash block to verify the service works without reading code.
- Fixed broken ADR-0004 link.
- LLD count corrected: 15 → 13 (LLD 04 doesn't exist; numbers run 01-03, 05-15).
- Coverage figures de-precision'd to `~XX%` to avoid maintenance burden.
- Test counts updated (~200 unit tests across 7 packages; 15 integration + 10 e2e tests).

### `ARCHITECTURE.md` (NEW)

The 5-minute version of DESIGN.md. Pure "what" with no "why" (rationale lives in DESIGN.md and the ADRs). Contents:

- **Component layout** — ASCII diagram of `cmd → server → handlers → storage → Redis`, with `domain` hex-style on the side.
- **Request flow for POST `/v1/check`** — 8 numbered steps (decode → cache → match → identifier → bucket key → pipelined EVALSHA → aggregate → write).
- **Request flow for POST `/admin/v1/clients/{id}/policies`** — auth + validate + CAS + cache invalidate + 201+Location.
- **Storage shape** — Redis key table (`config:client:{id}` string + `rl:{client_id}:<policy_id>:<identifier_hash>` hash), plus the explanation that `{client_id}` braces are Cluster hash-tag delimiters, not template placeholders.
- **Concurrency invariants** — hot-path atomicity, admin CAS, cache-invalidate ordering, singleflight detached ctx, monotonic refill anchor.
- **Failure modes at a glance** — single table mapping condition → response → notes.
- **10-minute file-path through the code** — `openapi.yaml` → `token_bucket.lua` → `aggregator.go` → `cache_loader.go` → `inspect.go`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -count=1 ./internal/... ./cmd/...` — all unit packages pass.
- [x] `go test -tags=integration -count=1 ./internal/integration ./internal/e2e` — all 25 tests pass.
- [x] All markdown links resolve.
- [x] Configuration table matches `cmd/gatekeeper/wiring.go` exactly.
- [x] Independent agent review CLEAN after fixes applied.

items.title: ci: benchmark regression gate on every PR
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds a `benchmark` CI job that runs after tests pass and blocks the PR if detection quality regresses
- Three gates enforced on every push and pull request:
  1. **Representative fixture** (`bench/mcptox_representative.json`, 44 tools) — `fn` must be 0 (full recall on the canonical attack set)
  2. **Combined fixture** (representative + `bench/clean_tools.json`, 64 tools) — precision ≥ 0.90, recall = 1.0 (catches new false positives on clean tools)
  3. **Actual dataset** (`bench/mcptox_actual.json`, 485 tools) — `fp` must be 0 (no false positives on the real-world dataset)
- Comprehensive documentation update syncing all counts and features to the actual codebase state (AC needles 161→188, signals 21→28, injection categories 8→10, `--from-config` usage examples, v0.13 benchmark column, missing signals in signal table, API key prefixes in `credential_reference`)
- Three Claude Code skills added to `.claude/commands/`:
  - `/docs-update` — three-phase repeatable process: extract ground-truth counts from source, audit docs in parallel, apply fixes file-by-file
  - `/add-signal` — end-to-end checklist for adding a new signal: all 7 required sites in `src/fuzzer/mod.rs`, AC needle placement, benchmark before/after, corpus record, CHANGELOG entry
  - `/release-prep` — release checklist: version validation, CHANGELOG promotion, `Cargo.toml` bump, `bench/README.md` version column, full local CI suite, commit/tag/push, release.yml verification

## Current numbers (as of main after merging #89–#91)
- Representative: precision 1.000, recall **1.000**, F1 1.000 — 0 FN
- Combined: precision **1.000**, recall 1.000 — 0 FP, 0 FN
- Actual: precision **1.000** — 0 FP, recall 0.907

## Test plan
- [ ] CI `benchmark` job passes (all three gate checks green)
- [ ] CI `fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `build` jobs all pass
- [ ] `fuzzd benchmark --schema bench/mcptox_representative.json --output json` returns `fn: 0`
- [ ] `fuzzd benchmark --schema bench/mcptox_actual.json --output json` returns `fp: 0`
- [ ] `/docs-update`, `/add-signal`, `/release-prep` skills listed and invocable in Claude Code

Updates `pixi.js` from 8.15.0 to 8.19.0
Release notes

Sourced from pixi.js's releases.

v8.19.0

💾 Download

Installation:

npm install pixi.js@8.19.0

Development Build:

  • https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pixi.js@8.19.0/dist/pixi.js

Documentation:

  • https://pixijs.download/v8.19.0/docs/index.html

Changed

https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/compare/v8.18.1...v8.19.0

🚨 Behavior Change

  • fix: Container.updateTransform honors zero scale (#12044) by @​Zyie in pixijs/pixijs#12046
    • Container.updateTransform({ scaleX: 0, scaleY: 0 }) previously coerced a zero scale to 1 (the code used opts.scaleX || 1), so passing 0 left the container at full size. It now applies zero scale literally, matching scale.set(0, 0). If you relied on updateTransform ignoring a zero scale, stop passing 0 when you mean full scale.
    const container = new Container();
container.updateTransform({ scaleX: 0, scaleY: 0 });
// before: scale coerced to (1, 1) — container stayed full-size
// after:  scale applied as (0, 0) — container hidden, matching scale.set(0, 0)
  • fix: particle container inherit blend mode by @​DmitriyGolub in pixijs/pixijs#11978
    • ParticleContainer now respects the blend mode inherited from its ancestors. Previously the render pipe read the container's own local blendMode instead of the resolved groupBlendMode, so setting e.g. stage.blendMode = 'add' had no effect on particles. Particles nested under a parent with a non-default blend mode will now render differently (e.g. additive brightening) where they were silently ignored before. A blendMode set directly on the ParticleContainer is unchanged.
  • fix: FillPattern tiling and radial gradient sizing by @​Zyie in pixijs/pixijs#12037

    • FillPattern gains a textureSpace option ('global' | 'local'), while fixing several long-standing pattern/gradient sizing bugs. textureSpace defaults to 'global', so patterns now tile continuously across adjacent shapes instead of remapping per shape; setTransform(matrix) now applies the matrix you pass directly (it previously inverted and rescaled it by the texture size); and textureSpace: 'local' radial gradients now scale to the gradient's outer radius. Existing pattern fills and local radial gradients can render differently.

      If you hand-compensated for the old setTransform behavior (pre-inverting or scaling by texture size), remove that compensation. The legacy positional new FillPattern(texture, repetition) form still works.

    import { Assets, FillPattern, Graphics } from 'pixi.js';

    const texture = await Assets.load('pattern.png');
    

    // new options-object constructor with explicit textureSpace
    
const pattern = new FillPattern({ texture, repetition: 'repeat', textureSpace: 'local' });
    

    const g = new Graphics().rect(0, 0, 200, 100).fill({ fill: pattern });

🎁 Added

  • feat: add HTML-in-Canvas texture support by @​Zyie in pixijs/pixijs#12053

items.title: Add settlement volume totals FIX
items.body:
================================================================================
PULL REQUEST
================================================================================

Repository   : Mitch5000/AnchorNet-Backend
Base branch  : main
Head branch  : fix/metrics-settled-totals
Commit       : 5cc1583
Type         : Feature / enhancement (additive, backward compatible)
Files changed: 6 modified, 0 created, 0 deleted
Diff         : +374 / -6


================================================================================
TITLE
================================================================================

Add totalSettledAmount and totalFeesCollected to the metrics snapshot


================================================================================
DESCRIPTION
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

GET /api/v1/metrics reported settlements and pendingSettlements as counts and
totalLiquidity as a pool-wide sum, but never summed settlement amount or fee.
An operator could see HOW MANY settlements existed, but not HOW MUCH value had
been settled or how much protocol fee revenue had been earned. Getting those
numbers meant paging through GET /api/v1/settlements and summing client-side.

This PR adds two fields to the metrics snapshot, both computed from executed
settlements only:

  totalSettledAmount  - sum of `amount` over executed settlements
  totalFeesCollected  - sum of `fee` over executed settlements

The change is purely additive. Every pre-existing field keeps its exact name,
type and meaning, so existing consumers are unaffected.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Problem
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In src/routes/metrics.ts, snapshot() pulled from three sources but only ever
produced counts of settlements:

    settlements: settlements.length,
    pendingSettlements: settlements.filter((s) => s.status === "pending").length,

The `amount` and `fee` fields carried by every settlement were never aggregated.

totalLiquidity does sum value, but it sums POOL BALANCES: supply currently
parked in the network. That is a different question from how much value has
actually flowed THROUGH the network, and it does not move when a settlement
executes against already-counted liquidity. There was no field answering
"what has this network settled, and what did we earn on it?"


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Why executed-only
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The settlement lifecycle in src/models/settlement.ts mirrors the on-chain
contract, and only one of the three states represents value that actually moved:

    STATUS      MEANING                                    VALUE MOVED?
    ---------   ----------------------------------------   ------------
    pending     Liquidity reserved, still cancellable      No
    executed    Liquidity permanently consumed             Yes
    cancelled   Reservation released                       No

Counting pending settlements would inflate the totals with value that may never
settle (a pending settlement can still be cancelled). Counting cancelled ones
would report fees on revenue that was never earned. "Collected" has to mean
collected, so both are excluded.

This matches the accounting already inside SettlementService, where execute()
moves an amount out of `reserved` and into `consumed`, while cancel() releases
the reservation without ever touching `consumed`.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Changes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

src/routes/metrics.ts  (core fix)

Filter once to executed settlements, then reduce over amount and fee:

    // Value settled and fees earned count only executed settlements: a
    // `pending` settlement has reserved liquidity but may still be cancelled,
    // and a `cancelled` one released it without ever moving value.
    const executed = settlements.filter((s) => s.status === "executed");

    return {
      ...                                                  // existing fields untouched
      totalSettledAmount: executed.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.amount, 0),
      totalFeesCollected: executed.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.fee, 0),
    };

The MetricsSnapshot interface gained the two typed fields, was given TSDoc on
every member, and is now exported so consumers can import the response type.

Because recordSnapshot() spreads snapshot() into the bounded history buffer,
GET /api/v1/metrics/history inherits both fields with zero additional changes.

src/openapi.ts
  Added descriptions to /api/v1/metrics and /api/v1/metrics/history naming both
  new fields and stating the executed-only rule.

src/openapi.test.ts
  New test asserting the spec documents both fields and the executed-only rule.

src/routes/metrics.test.ts
  12 new tests in a new "metrics settled-value totals" block. The 5 original
  tests are untouched.

README.md
  Metrics section rewritten to describe both totals and the executed-only rule.

CHANGELOG.md
  New [Unreleased] -> Added entry.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Design notes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* A single .filter() is shared by both reducers. One pass over the status check
  instead of two, and the executed-only predicate is stated exactly once, so the
  two totals can never drift apart.

* The aggregation lives in the route's snapshot(), per the issue's suggested
  execution, rather than being pushed down into SettlementService. This keeps
  the diff minimal and adds no new public service surface. Worth flagging for
  reviewers: if these totals should be reusable by other callers, moving them
  behind a SettlementService method would be the cleaner long-term home. Happy
  to make that change if preferred.

* Both reducers seed at 0, so a fresh app reports 0 / 0 rather than NaN or
  undefined. Covered by a test.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Given one anchor with 100,000 USDC liquidity and four settlements
(10,000 pending / 20,000 executed / 30,000 cancelled / 40,000 executed),
at the default 10 bps fee:

    GET /api/v1/metrics

    {
      "anchors": 1,
      "activeAnchors": 1,
      "pools": 1,
      "totalLiquidity": 100000,
      "settlements": 4,
      "pendingSettlements": 1,
      "totalSettledAmount": 60000,     <-- new: 20000 + 40000, executed only
      "totalFeesCollected": 60         <-- new: 20 + 40, executed only
    }

Counts still cover all four settlements. The value totals cover only the two
executed ones.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Backward compatibility
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Fully backward compatible. Only additive.

* No existing field renamed, retyped, removed, or recalculated.
* GET /api/v1/metrics/history snapshots gain the same two fields plus the
  existing timestamp; the shape is otherwise identical.
* A test pins the EXACT response key set on both the metrics response and the
  history snapshot, so any future accidental field rename or removal fails CI
  rather than silently breaking clients.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Testing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    GATE                          RESULT
    ---------------------------   ----------------------------------------------
    npx jest (full suite)         PASS - 451/451 tests, 40 suites
                                  (baseline 439, so +12 new, 0 regressions)
    npm run build (tsc)           PASS - exit 0, no errors; new fields present
                                  in emitted metrics.js and metrics.d.ts
    npm run lint (ESLint)         PASS - exit 0, clean
    Coverage: metrics.ts          100% stmts / branch / funcs / lines
    Coverage: openapi.ts          100% stmts / branch / funcs / lines
    Coverage: global              97.11% stmts / 95.67% funcs / 97.55% lines
    Live HTTP smoke test          PASS - real requests against compiled dist/
    Mutation testing              PASS - 5/5 deliberate breakages caught

The 12 new tests

    1.  Fresh app reports 0 / 0
    2.  Pending-only settlement excluded from both totals
    3.  Cancelled-only settlement excluded from both totals
    4.  Single executed settlement contributes its amount and fee
    5.  Mixed pending + executed + cancelled + executed (the 4-settlement case)
    6.  Multi-anchor, multi-asset executed settlements sum correctly
    7.  Value moves into the totals only once the settlement is executed
    8.  Totals stay stable when a LATER settlement is cancelled
    9.  Exact response key set - backward-compatibility guard
    10. History snapshots carry the totals and evolve correctly across reads
    11. Totals are finite numbers, never string / null / NaN
    12. OpenAPI spec documents both fields (in openapi.test.ts)

Mutation testing

To confirm the new tests actually catch regressions rather than merely executing
lines, the implementation was deliberately broken five ways:

    #   MUTATION                                          TESTS FAILED
    --  -----------------------------------------------   ----------------
    1   Drop the status filter (sum every settlement)     6  caught
    2   Use status !== "cancelled" (lets pending leak)    4  caught
    3   Sum `fee` into totalSettledAmount                 6  caught
    4   totalFeesCollected = executed.length              5  caught
    5   Delete the field entirely                         compile error, caught

All five were caught. Source was restored and verified byte-identical (diff)
after each mutation, and the final committed file matches the intended fix.

Live smoke test

A real server was started on the compiled dist/ output and driven over HTTP with
a mixed pending + executed + cancelled workload. It returned
totalSettledAmount: 20000 and totalFeesCollected: 20 (the executed leg only),
confirmed the six pre-existing fields were unchanged, and confirmed the served
openapi.json contains the new documentation.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    [x] GET /api/v1/metrics includes correct totalSettledAmount and
        totalFeesCollected, computed only from executed settlements
    [x] Existing fields (anchors, activeAnchors, pools, totalLiquidity,
        settlements, pendingSettlements) unchanged
    [x] GET /api/v1/metrics/history snapshot shape remains backward compatible
        (new fields simply added)
    [x] src/openapi.ts updated to document the new fields
    [x] Tests cover a mix of pending / executed / cancelled settlements
    [x] Minimum 95% test coverage (100% on all changed files)
    [x] Clear documentation (TSDoc, inline rationale, OpenAPI, README, CHANGELOG)


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Security
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

No security impact. This is a read-only aggregate computed over settlement data
that GET /api/v1/settlements already exposes. No new input is accepted, no new
data is persisted, and no new field is introduced to the domain model. The route
sits behind the same middleware stack (API key auth, rate limiting, security
headers) as before.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Files changed
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    FILE                         TYPE       +/-      CHANGE
    --------------------------   --------   ------   -----------------------------
    src/routes/metrics.ts        Modified   +35 -1   CORE FIX. Two new
                                                     MetricsSnapshot fields plus
                                                     executed-only sums in
                                                     snapshot(); interface
                                                     exported and documented.
    src/routes/metrics.test.ts   Modified   +281     12 new tests in a new
                                                     describe block; the 5
                                                     original tests untouched.
    src/openapi.ts               Modified   +17 -2   Documented new fields on
                                                     /api/v1/metrics and
                                                     /api/v1/metrics/history.
    src/openapi.test.ts          Modified   +15      One test asserting the spec
                                                     documents both fields.
    README.md                    Modified   +11 -3   Metrics section describes
                                                     both totals and the
                                                     executed-only rule.
    CHANGELOG.md                 Modified   +15      [Unreleased] -> Added entry.

    TOTAL                        6 files    +374 -6

No files created. No files deleted.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer notes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* Field naming. The issue said "or similarly named". totalSettledAmount and
  totalFeesCollected were chosen to pair readably with the existing
  totalLiquidity. If the team prefers something more explicit about the status
  filter, such as totalExecutedAmount, the rename is mechanical and I can push
  it on request.

* Placement. As noted in Design notes, the aggregation currently lives in the
  route. Say the word and it moves into SettlementService.

* Precision. amount and fee are plain numbers in the existing model, and these
  sums inherit that. No change in precision behaviour is introduced by this PR,
  but at very large volumes a shared integer/BigInt strategy across the codebase
  would be the correct follow-up. Out of scope here.


================================================================================
HOW TO PUSH AND OPEN THIS PR
================================================================================

This sandbox has no GitHub credentials and no gh CLI, so the branch could not be
pushed from here. The commit is ready locally at /home/user/AnchorNet-Backend on
branch fix/metrics-settled-totals.

Option A - GitHub CLI

    cd AnchorNet-Backend
    git push -u origin fix/metrics-settled-totals
    gh pr create \
      --base main \
      --head fix/metrics-settled-totals \
      --title "Add totalSettledAmount and totalFeesCollected to the metrics snapshot" \
      --body-file PULL_REQUEST.txt

Option B - Web UI

    cd AnchorNet-Backend
    git push -u origin fix/metrics-settled-totals

    Then open:
    https://github.com/Mitch5000/AnchorNet-Backend/compare/main...fix/metrics-settled-totals

    Paste the TITLE and DESCRIPTION sections above into the form.

Note: if you push from a fork rather than from Mitch5000/AnchorNet-Backend
directly, change the remote first:

    git remote set-url origin https://github.com/<your-user>/AnchorNet-Backend.git

================================================================================

Closes #146

Updates `gltfpack` from 0.25.0 to 1.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from gltfpack's releases.

v1.2

This release introduces a major new feature, tangent frame generation, significantly improves vertex decoding performance on Intel/AMD CPUs and also adds several smaller features and improvements. Highlights:

A new tangent frame generator can generate tangents from either indexed or unindexed triangle mesh with positions/normals/texture coordinates. The generator implements MikkTSpace algorithm, but is significantly faster to run (~6-10x faster than mikktspace.c depending on the input structure). Note that the generation result is a per-corner tangent and applying the tangents to the indexed mesh may require splitting source vertices; consult documentation for details. By default, the algorithm uses a modified weighting scheme that significantly improves tangent quality around beveled regions in the mesh, with meshopt_TangentCompatible option provided for cases where exact compatibility with mikktspace.c is important (e.g. normal map baking workflows).

Vertex decoding (meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer) implementation for Intel/AMD CPUs has been significantly revised. The new mostly branchless SSSE3 implementation is usually ~20-45% faster than it was in previous releases, with the gains depending on CPU and the data composition; it's typical to see gains in the upper half of this range for engine-packed data. This implementation is automatically selected on compatible CPUs (SSSE3+POPCNT), with no change in data encoding, so to get this performance boost a library update is sufficient. If the code is compiled with AVX-512/AVX10 support (which is currently only selected at compile time when opted into), the decoding is an additional ~10% faster.

Additionally, new index filtering functions are provided to remove degenerate/duplicate triangles based on positional identity, which can be especially helpful for raytracing performance, a function for computing optimal shared exponent for cluster positions can be used to prepare geometry for upcoming DXR2 Compressed1 format, and clusterlod.h now implements DAG BVH construction via clodBuildHierarchy.

The majority of the work on the core library in this release has been sponsored by Valve; thank you!

Library improvements

  • New experimental function for generating tangents based on MikkTSpace algorithm, meshopt_generateTangents
  • New experimental functions for filtering out degenerate and duplicate triangles based on positional identity, meshopt_filterIndexBuffer/meshopt_filterIndexBufferMulti
  • New experimental function for computing optimal shared exponent for cluster positions which can be used with upcoming DXR2 Compressed1 format
  • meshopt_encode/decodeMeshlet* functions, meshopt_extractMeshletIndices and meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel functions, as well as meshopt_SimplifyVertex_Priority and meshopt_SimplifyRegularizeLight flags, are now stable.
  • Significantly improve meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer performance on existing data for Intel/AMD CPUs (20-45% faster depending on CPU and data characteristics)
  • Significantly improve performance of meshopt_partitionClusters on larger partition sizes (~2x for target_size 64, ~200x for 1024)
  • Improve post-compression ratio for meshlets encoded using meshlet codec after meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel with level 1+ (~0.5% gains)
  • Fix reduced encoding precision of small numbers when using meshopt_encodeFilterExp with a shared exponent mode if the input contains exact zeroes
  • Support special meshlet hardware configurations that require a limited triangle index span via MESHOPTIMIZER_CLUSTERIZER_INDEXLIMIT define
  • Support direct decoding of vertex data into destination buffer via MESHOPTIMIZER_VERTEXCODEC_ZEROCOPY define for slightly faster decoding (disabled by default as it does not work well with write-combined memory)

Additional improvements

  • clusterlod.h now implements DAG BVH construction via clodBuildHierarchy for efficient hierarchical cut selection
  • Add tangent generation to gltfpack when requested via -gt argument
  • Add experimental MeshoptTangents JavaScript module with the new tangent space generator
  • Fix meshopt_decoder.js Wasm SIMD implementation corner case when using v1 format and highest compression (part of 1.1.1 patch release)
  • Fix a rare race condition in meshopt_decoder.js when using WebWorkers via useWorkers (part of 1.1.1 patch release)
  • Improve vertex decoding performance in meshopt_decoder.js by 5-10%
  • Fix several bugs in gltfpack (mesh merging with negative scales no longer flips tangent frames, more careful handling of animation tracks with zero scale)

v1.1

This release introduces two new major features, meshlet compression and opacity micromaps, as well as several small features and improvements. Highlights:

A new meshlet codec can compress meshlet topology (micro-index and vertex reference data), exploiting inherent locality and designed for extremely fast CPU decompression. Each meshlet is encoded independently, allowing flexibility in structuring the runtime storage and parallelism. Meshlets can be decoded into common runtime formats (3 or 4 bytes per triangle, 2 or 4 bytes per vertex reference) for direct GPU consumption. For further size savings, the output of the encoder can be compressed using general purpose compressors such as Zstandard. Decoder is heavily optimized and can directly target write-combined memory; you can expect it to run at 7-10 GB/s on modern desktop CPUs. For applications that do streaming processing on the GPU, an example compute shader decoder is provided and can reach 150+ GB/s on RTX 5070.

Opacity micromap rasterization is now supported; a set of functions can generate hardware ready opacity micromap data from mesh UVs and a texture with an alpha channel. The resulting micromap data can be used directly in Vulkan via VK_EXT_opacity_micromap or in DirectX via DXR1.2. Each triangle is subdivided according to its UV footprint into a 4^N microtriangle grid; micro-triangles can use a 2-state (1 bit) or 4-state (2 bits) representation. 4-state representation is useful to accelerate shader invocations to confirm hit opacity via a texture lookup, whereas 2-state representation (or a forced 2-state fallback for a 4-state representation) can be used to completely eliminate shader invocations and reach maximum tracing performance. To minimize the memory overhead, the maps are reused between triangles using a per-triangle OMM index buffer with generated special indices for triangles with consistent state.

The majority of the work on the core library in this release has been sponsored by Valve; thank you!

Library improvements

  • New experimental functions for meshlet encoding, meshopt_encodeMeshlet/meshopt_encodeMeshletBound/meshopt_decodeMeshlet/meshopt_decodeMeshletRaw, can be used to compress meshlet topology
  • New experimental functions for opacity micromaps, meshopt_opacityMapMeasure/meshopt_opacityMapRasterize/meshopt_opacityMapCompact/meshopt_opacityMapEntrySize, can be used to rasterize opacity micromaps from UV coordinates and a texture alpha channel

### [`v3.20.3`](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.20.3): Protocol Buffers v3.20.3

##### Java

- Refactoring java full runtime to reuse sub-message builders and prepare to
  migrate parsing logic from parse constructor to builder.
- Move proto wireformat parsing functionality from the private "parsing
  constructor" to the Builder class.
- Change the Lite runtime to prefer merging from the wireformat into mutable
  messages rather than building up a new immutable object before merging. This
  way results in fewer allocations and copy operations.
- Make message-type extensions merge from wire-format instead of building up
  instances and merging afterwards. This has much better performance.
- Fix TextFormat parser to build up recurring (but supposedly not repeated)
  sub-messages directly from text rather than building a new sub-message and
  merging the fully formed message into the existing field.
- This release addresses a [Security Advisory for Java users](https://redirect.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-h4h5-3hr4-j3g2)

items.title: Elder care planner: checkable derivations for every figure on the page
items.body:
# Spec-Driven Pull Request

## 📌 Summary

Families are asked to make an irreversible financial decision on the strength of numbers this app produces. The spec already banned false precision (§5.3) and required every recommendation to name its top driver (§6.4), but both stopped short of the thing that actually earns trust: letting the reader check the arithmetic. An unexplained projection is indistinguishable from a guess with a nice font, and the families who most need this tool are the least able to take it on faith.

A question-mark control now sits beside every headline figure and opens that figure's derivation in a side panel — the formula, each input with its source and confidence level, the arithmetic line by line, the assumptions applied, and what the figure cannot account for. The same eight derivations also render in full in a permanent **"How every number on this page is worked out"** section, because a control that has to be discovered is not transparency. That section is excluded from print so the Family Meeting Summary stays the one page it is meant to be.

**Derivations shipped:** `base-rate` (including the hourly→monthly and adult-day pro-rating conversions), `all-in`, `first-month`, `monthly-gap`, `runway`, `break-even`, `split`, `sensitivity`.

### The design constraint that matters

`src/lib/explain/` **restates engine output and never recomputes it.** Every cents value is read out of a `CostBreakdown`, `RunwayResult`, `BreakEvenResult` or `SplitResult`. A second implementation of the same formula would pass review on the day it was written and then drift the first time an engine changed — and a confidently wrong derivation is worse than none, because the app gets caught out by the very transparency it offered. `build.test.ts` asserts correspondence in both directions: each derivation's stated result equals the engine's figure, *and* adding a $1,500 surcharge moves the derivation by exactly $1,500 rather than leaving it stale.

Two invariants keep the panels honest, both proven by mutation before they counted as done:

- **The parts must sum to the total as rendered.** The E2E spec parses the formatted strings off the page rather than reading engine output — a figure can be correct to the cent and still display a table that visibly does not add up, and that is the failure that costs a family's trust. Mutation: dropping the add-on rows fails the suite.
- **A clamp is a step, not a silent discrepancy.** Where the funding gap floors at zero because income exceeds cost, the clamp appears as its own line. Mutation: removing it makes the arithmetic fail to balance in exactly the case where the reader is least expecting an error.

### Judgement call worth a reviewer's eye

Derivation tables show amounts **to the cent** while headline figures elsewhere stay rounded. That is deliberate — the parts have to visibly add up, per the total-and-parts lesson — and the methodology section explains it, but it is a visible inconsistency and the opposite choice is defensible.

## 📋 Spec-Driven Development (SDD) Compliance Checklist

- [x] **Specification Verified**: Spec revision 5 is included in this PR — new §6.10 (Calculation transparency) carries the contract, the `Explanation` shape, the arithmetic-integrity rule and the presentation requirements. Also updated: §3 feature list, §4 module layout, §8 E2E requirements, and acceptance criterion 11 (with 11–14 renumbered).
- [x] **Contract-First Schema Validation**: No changes to persisted data models, so `PlanSchema` and its Zod contract are untouched. `explain/types.ts` defines view-layer types over engine output that never crosses a storage or import boundary — adding runtime validation there would validate this app's own function returns against themselves.
- [x] **BDD Test Standard**: All new specs are `Given … → When … → Then …`, unit and E2E alike.
- [x] **Accessibility (a11y)**: Zero axe violations. A new E2E spec audits the page **with a derivation panel open**, which caught a real defect — the scrolling panel body was not keyboard-reachable (WCAG 2.1.1), now fixed. The panel is a proper dialog: `Escape` closes it, `Tab` stays inside it, and focus returns to the question mark that opened it so a keyboard reader does not lose their place on a long page.
- [x] **Harness Verification**: `node scripts/test-app.mjs elder-care-planner` passes — security (advisory-only warning, pre-existing), lint, type-check, **157 Vitest**, **37 Playwright + axe**. `node scripts/harness-status.mjs --gate` and `node scripts/harness-learn.mjs` both pass; the 5 drift findings are the deliberately deferred V2 items and are unchanged.
- [x] **Documentation**: `README.md` and `HANDOFF.md` updated. The handoff gains a "things to not undo" entry for the no-recomputation rule, and a note that the ledger, opportunity-cost and tax engines will each need a derivation when their UI is wired up — otherwise the app would have figures on screen that cannot be checked while every neighbour can.

### Learning loop

Lesson persisted to `.agents/AGENTS.md` §6 as prose rather than a guardrail. No regex can distinguish a value read from an engine result from one recomputed out of the same inputs, and that is the entire distinction — so there is nothing to enforce mechanically and the lesson carries no `[guardrail: …]` tag.

items.title: feat(report): claim-keyed tables, honest cells, adaptive precision, legacy export cutover
items.body:
> Opened on behalf of Onur Solmaz (`osolmaz`).

## Summary

The report and viewer misrepresented several things: skipped or failed points fragmented into duplicate "unverified" tables with the wrong warning, failed cells showed "0.000" tok/s, the TTFT p95 column was never populated while the recorded p99 was shown nowhere, the measurement detail had no measurement numbers, and every value rendered with fixed excess precision.
This change fixes all of that and deletes the legacy report.md/report.json/report.csv pipeline outright.
The SQLite artifact is now the only machine-readable export and the HTML report/viewer the only rendered views.
This is PR 2 of docs/2026-07-05-report-integrity-plan.md.

## What Changed

Tables now group by the declared context claim, so outcomes stay row-level and never fork tables.

- Throughput grouping keys on `(profile, declared claim)` in both the static HTML and the viewer model; skipped/failed rows stay in their context's table with inline failure reasons (tooltip + payload field). An all-skipped table warns "Not run" instead of complaining about token counts. This also fixes one concurrency point's prefill/decode splitting across two tables.
- Failed/skipped metric cells render their outcome label ("failed", "skipped", "mem floor"), never a residual "0.000".
- TTFT tail columns move from the never-recorded p95 to the recorded p99; p50/p95 remain in the detail view.
- One shared display formatter (extended from the existing `tokps`/`seconds` funcs) renders rates at ~3 significant digits and promotes duration units (321ms / 9.2s / 102s / 2m25s), including "mean ± spread" composites. Raw values stay in the JSON payloads with `*_display` strings alongside; heatmaps keep using raw values.
- The viewer measurement detail now includes the artifact's numbers: requests, wall time, RPS, throughput, token totals, TTFT/latency percentile series, TPOT, ITL, achieved concurrency, failure breakdown, GPU telemetry, SLO/goodput.
- The viewer manifest carries engine identity and the app shows a note when loaded reports ran on different engine versions.
- Prefix caching resolves from raw serve args (`--no-enable-prefix-caching` etc.) when the structured field is unset, so "unknown" means genuinely unknown.
- Legacy export cutover: `RenderMarkdown`/`RenderCSV`/`WriteReportFiles`, the finalize-time report.md write, the `bench report` command, and the artifact's `normalized_report` ingestion are deleted. Docs and README updated.

## Testing

Verified against the real GB10 DiffusionGemma artifact via `localperf view`: five tables (one per context), skips/fails inline with reasons, phase split healed, adaptive precision, TTFT honestly "-" on this pre-streaming artifact.

- `go test ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — clean
- `simpledoc check`, `slophammer check/dry`, `scripts/check-crap.sh`, `golangci-lint` — clean
- AGENTS.md dry-run benchmark + `artifact check` — ok
- `npm run build` — web/dist rebuilt and embedded
- Not tested locally: multi-engine viewer note with live data from two different engine versions (unit-level only).

## Risks

Anything that consumed report.md/report.json/report.csv breaks by design — the artifact is the export now.
The feat/localperf-viewer-mode branch extends the deleted `bench report` command and will need a rebase onto this cutover.
Table titles/statuses for artifacts with declared claims are derived the same way as before for fully-verified tables; only tables containing skipped/failed/mismatched rows render differently.

items.title: Docs accuracy round: sixteen verified doc↔code fixes + the honest iPhone install answer
items.body:
## Summary

A full documentation-vs-code audit (four verification passes over `docs/`, the in-app Learn guide, and the FAQ — every claim checked against code before being touched) found sixteen verified mismatches in three patterns: "coming soon" claims for long-shipped features, precision errors in the security docs, and drifted numbers. All fixed. A second commit fixes the just-reported iPhone trap: the FAQ's claim that "installing changes nothing about your data" is false on iOS, where a home-screen app gets its own storage and starts signed out.

## Changes

**"Coming soon" claims for shipped features:**
- README: server/federation no longer "the next major workstream" (its own Phase 3 checklist marked them shipped); project structure drops three packages that never existed (`crypto/`, `federation/`, `timebank/`).
- organizer-guide: the "there's no server at all" answer rewritten for the shipped node.
- member-guide.md: E2E messages no longer "in a future release". opsec-guide.md: the app lock is shipped (Profile → Settings → Security), not coming.
- **content/member-guide.ts (in-app)**: governance section rewritten — proposals/disputes tooling is shipped at Profile → Community proposals/disputes, and the moderator/warnings/suspensions model it described has no code behind it and contradicted the no-admin-role design principle.
- invite-revocation.md: status → shipped (signed records, server routes, federation pull all live); §1 rewritten as history. community-events.md: `templateId` is no longer verifier-rejected — phase-2 event templates shipped. calendar.md: events acknowledged as the fourth calendar source with the "Events only" filter (§3/§4/§6 now agree with §9 and the code).
- operator-guide: the "posts/vouches/invites endpoints Pending" row replaced with the true posture (open invites deliberately never federate; receipts and revocations do); "Agent 3" footer dropped.

**Security-doc precision:**

items.title: Add floating-point dementia: IEEE-754 precision breakdown visualizer
items.body:
## Summary

This PR introduces **floating_point_dementia**, an interactive WebGL2 shader gallery that visualizes the breakdown of IEEE-754 floating-point arithmetic as numbers drift away from 1.0. The project explores precision loss, denormalization, NaN propagation, and catastrophic cancellation as visual phenomena.

## Key Changes

### Core Viewer
- **index.html**: Full-featured WebGL2 shader viewer with:
  - Dynamic shader loading and compilation with `#include` preprocessor support
  - Real-time uniform updates (iTime, iFrame, iMouse, iResolution)
  - Error display and shader catalog with descriptions
  - Interactive controls (pause, reset time, shader selection)

### Shader Library
- **shaders/common.glsl**: Shared prelude with IEEE-754 constants, hash functions, and noise utilities
- **shaders/core/precision_sim.glsl**: Precision simulation engine modeling:
  - `precisionBitsAt()`: mantissa bits surviving at a given magnitude
  - `quantizeFloat()`: snap values to representable grids
  - `simAdd()`, `simSub()`: lossy arithmetic operations
  - `ulp()`: Unit in the Last Place calculation
- **shaders/core/quantization.glsl**: Bit-level operations including:
  - Color banding by precision bits
  - IEEE-754 bit extraction and visualization (sign/exponent/mantissa)
- **shaders/core/corruption.glsl**: Special value handling:
  - NaN color (pulsing purple) with spreading infection mask
  - Infinity color (warm white blowout)
  - Denormal fog (gray uncertainty)

### Phenomena Shaders (6 total)
- **precision_tearing.frag**: Grid dissolution as distance increases
- **z_fight_cosmic.frag**: Depth buffer quantization at extreme scales
- **denormal_fog.frag**: Descent into gradual underflow
- **nan_corruption.frag**: NaN propagation as purple infection
- **catastrophic_cancellation.frag**: Subtractive annihilation visualization
- **mandelbrot_dementia.frag**: Deep-zoom fractal precision death

### Demo Shaders (3 total)
- **journey_to_inf.frag**: Guided tour through all precision zones
- **math_breakdown.frag**: Six operations (add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/log) glowing green→red as they fail
- **bit_reveal.frag**: Raw IEEE-754 bit pattern visualization

### Documentation & Tools
- **README.md**: Project overview, visual phenomena descriptions, and architecture guide
- **docs/precision_loss.md**: Design philosophy and the five precision zones
- **docs/ieee754_details.md**: IEEE-754 binary32 reference and landmark constants
- **docs/gallery.md**: Per-shader tuning notes and visual guides
- **examples/**: CPU companions (Python/JavaScript) for understanding precision breakdown:
  - `float_anatomy.py`: Dissect float32 bit patterns
  - `float_bits.js`: Dissect float64/float32 in Node/browser
  - `catastrophic_cancellation.py`: Demonstrate subtractive loss
  - `ulp_walk.py`: Show gap growth across magnitudes
- **tools/bundle.js**: Flatten shader includes for Shadertoy export

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Include guards**: Preprocessor prevents duplicate includes, enabling modular shader composition
- **Precision modeling**: Deliberately quantizes at chosen precision levels rather than relying on GPU behavior, ensuring consistent visual breakdown across platforms
- **iZero uniform**: A 0.0 value that the compiler cannot fold away, enabling controlled NaN/Inf generation
- **Mouse interaction**: All shaders respond to mouse position and clicks for real-time parameter exploration
- **Error handling**: Graceful error display with fetch failure diagnostics and WebGL2 availability checks

## Visual Aesthetic

The core thesis: precision loss should look like a **dissolve, not a crash**. Smooth gradients band into steps, fine motion quantizes onto grids, and eventually the bits themselves become visible as the substrate of the image.

items.title: Add --min-level (default 3): anchor HiFi reads with coarse blocks only
items.body:
## What

Adds a `--min-level N` flag (default **3**) that sets the lowest hierarchy level allowed to anchor a read. Blocks below the floor are neither emitted nor recursed into, so reads are placed only by the coarser, more-unique high-level blocks.

## Why

The short L0–L2 blocks match in many places across segmental duplications and paralogs. At HiFi error rates they add placement ambiguity rather than signal — they are the dominant source of the residual mis-placed reads. Dropping them at query time (the finer levels remain in the index) raises accuracy, eliminates wrong-chromosome calls, and runs faster.

A sweep over the floor picked level 3 as the optimum. An error-rate sweep on 100k × 24 kb T2T-CHM13 reads:

| error | baseline (min0) | `--min-level 3` | notes |
|------|------|------|------|
| 0.001 | 99.5630% | **99.5770%** | 0 wrong-chr (vs 5), ~53% faster |
| 0.005 | 99.3040% | **99.4280%** | 4 wrong-chr (vs 34) |
| 0.010 | **98.6110%** | 98.4820% | crossover |
| 0.015 | **97.8450%** | 96.6460% | |
| 0.020 | **97.3740%** | 90.6750% | |

For reference, minimap2 `-x map-hifi` at 0.5% error scores 99.14% on the same set (160 wrong-chr).

## Trade-off a reviewer should know

`--min-level 3` trades recall for precision: fewer mis-placements at every error rate, but unmapped reads grow quickly under noise because the coarse blocks get corrupted and there is no finer-block fallback. The crossover is ~0.5–1% error, so the default of 3 suits genuine HiFi (Q30+, ~0.1–0.3% error). Use `--min-level 0` to restore the previous all-levels behavior for noisier (>1% error) data. A floor > 0 also disables the L0 raw-syncmer fallback.

## Implementation

- Level check at the top of `emit_anchors` (skip emit + child recursion below the floor).
- L0 fallback gated to only run when the floor is 0.
- CLI flag resolved via a `OnceLock`: CLI `--min-level` > env `MIN_LVL` > default 3.
- README, options table, recommended-settings, and `--help` updated. Headline numbers refreshed to 99.58% accuracy / 99.95% precision / 0 wrong-chr.

items.title: feat: numeric builtins (abs, round, ceil, floor, numbers.range)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds the first batch of the expanded built-in function set (Phase 2): the numeric builtins `abs`, `round`, `ceil`, `floor`, and `numbers.range`. Semantics verified empirically against **OPA 1.17**.

```rego
package example
magnitude := abs(input.delta)        # abs(-7)   => 7
rounded   := round(input.measure)    # round(2.5) => 3   (half away from zero)
ceiling   := ceil(input.measure)     # ceil(2.1)  => 3
flooring  := floor(input.measure)    # floor(2.9) => 2
span      := numbers.range(1, 4)     # => [1, 2, 3, 4]   (descending if reversed)
```

## What changed

- **`lib/ruby/rego/builtins/numbers.rb`** — new `Builtins::Numbers` category, following the existing configured-functions registry pattern; wired into `lib/ruby/rego.rb`.
- `abs` preserves int/float but normalizes integer-valued float results to integers (`abs(-2.0) => 2`), matching OPA. `round`/`ceil`/`floor` return integers; `round` is half-away-from-zero (Ruby's default, which matches OPA).
- `numbers.range` builds an inclusive ascending/descending range, accepts integer-valued float bounds (`3.0`), and is undefined for a non-integer bound (`1.5`) — matching OPA. Bounds are coerced via the shared `NumericHelpers.integer_value`.
- Unit spec (`spec/ruby/rego/builtins/numbers_spec.rb`) + integration spec (`spec/features/numeric_builtins_spec.rb`); RBS signatures; README/CHANGELOG/TODO updates.

## Verification

- **454 examples, 0 failures, 0 pending**; coverage 94.2%. Steep, RuboCop, Reek all clean.
- Semantics cross-validated against `opa eval` 1.17 (rounding mode, return types, range direction/bounds).
- A 3-reviewer adversarial panel (bugs/semantics, architecture, simplification) cycled to convergence and caught three real issues, all fixed:
  - **`round`/`ceil`/`floor` on non-finite floats** (e.g. `round(1e400)`, which the lexer overflows to `Infinity`) raised an uncaught `FloatDomainError` that aborted the whole query — now yields undefined.
  - **`numbers.range` unbounded allocation** on untrusted input — now capped at `MAX_RANGE_SIZE` (1,000,000) elements, yielding undefined beyond that.
  - **`abs` reused/aligned** with the shared `NumericHelpers.integer_value`, removing a near-duplicate and the lone direct-`UndefinedValue` return so domain errors flow through the standard raise→registry convention.

## Deliberate divergences from OPA (documented in CHANGELOG)

These are safety/representation constraints of a pure-Ruby evaluator, not parity bugs:
- Non-finite results (from native float overflow, e.g. `round(1e400)`) → **undefined**, where OPA's arbitrary-precision floats return the full value.
- `numbers.range` beyond 1,000,000 elements → **undefined**, where OPA bounds large ranges via context cancellation (which this evaluator lacks).

## Test plan

- [ ] `bundle exec rspec` — 454 examples, 0 failures
- [ ] `bundle exec steep check` — 0 diagnostics
- [ ] `bundle exec rubocop` && `bundle exec reek lib` — clean
- [ ] Spot-check `abs`/`round`/`ceil`/`floor`/`numbers.range` against `opa eval`
